summary: 80 game ideas generated from four different angles, scored by two independent judges, the top 12 attacked by two critics, and the survivors rebuilt with the critics' fixes. Everything is here, including what was cut and why.

method.detail: Four generators, 20 ideas each, from different angles: satisfying actions × cozy fantasies; culture signals; games built to spread through links and video; contrarian ideas and unmet needs. Each was told to push past its first ideas and avoid reskins.

Two judges scored every idea 1–5 on originality, 5-second clarity, clip appeal, built-in spread, solo buildability, demand and money. One judged as a player; the other as a veteran designer looking for ideas that die after five minutes. Their totals rarely differed by more than a few points.

A player and market critic asked what brings people back on day two, what the first frame of the clip is, and who already makes it. A build and distribution critic checked phone-browser limits (camera, mic, storage inside TikTok's browser), servers, art load, privacy and abuse.
The five strongest were rewritten as full plans with the critics' fixes built in, then scored on the same factors as every other suggestion, including originality and fit for a solo creator.

cutLessons: One-time novelty was the most common killer: lots of ideas are delightful for five minutes and have no reason to return (one leaf pile, one perfect peel, one soap shaving).
Gift-by-link toys spread easily but often give each player a single action; the survivors add a collection, a keepsake or a daily reason to come back.
Ideas that need many strangers online at once (shared rivers, lit windows, public streets) can't be seeded by one creator at launch.
Ideas that need people together at the same moment (relay chains, real-time pairing) lose most players at the hand-off.
Money was the weakest score almost everywhere; most ideas fall back on a generic small unlock.
Phone browsers inside TikTok and Instagram make camera and microphone unreliable, which hurt several otherwise strong ideas.

ideas.title: Lemon Ink
ideas.hook: Iron a crumpled note until the secret message appears. Then send one.
ideas.oneLiner: Smooth out crumpled, coffee-stained notes with a warm iron; heat slowly reveals lemon-juice writing. Write your own hidden note and send it as a link: your friend has to iron it to read it.
ideas.fantasy: Night-shift clerk at a village dead-letter office, and secret-note passer between friends
ideas.coreLoop: Drag the iron over crumpled paper; wrinkles flatten with paper physics and soft hiss, heat brings up the hidden ink stroke by stroke; the revealed note moves a little neighbourhood story along and unlocks the next crumpled letter.
ideas.howItSpreads: The share IS the game: 'I left you a secret note' link opens a crumpled paper only the friend can iron open (ideal for group chats, Valentine's, birthdays, crushes). Clip: a crumpled ball unfolding and brown words blooming under the iron, filmed without sound. Reply-with-a-note creates chains.
ideas.monetization: Free notes; $3 supporter pack with stationery (airmail, recipe card, school-notebook paper), ink types (milk ink, invisible UV), wax seals, and a cat paw-print signature; seasonal paper packs.
ideas.whatsNew: A reveal verb (heat-ironing) that doubles as a private message format; the game is a delivery mechanism for real feelings, not a skin on a genre.
ideas.closestExisting: No ironing/invisible-ink game found; nearest are scratch-card reveal apps and Kind Words (anonymous letters). Difference: tactile reveal + addressed to a friend you know.
ideas.buildNotes: Very feasible: a mesh-deformed paper texture whose wrinkle normal map fades under the cursor, plus a shader that darkens text by accumulated heat. Text is typography/handwriting fonts, so almost no bespoke art: 5-6 paper textures, an iron sprite, a cat. Messages stored in the URL (compressed) so no server or moderation needed at first; add preset-phrase mode for younger players.
cultureSignals: Unboxing / mystery-reveal as a content format
Loneliness epidemic and the search for low-cost third places
ideas.verdictA: New reveal verb that is itself a message format; URL-stored notes, no server; group-chat native.
ideas.verdictB: Share-as-message is native and charming, but it's a greeting-card toy; little reason to return between notes.
ideas.whySurvived: Ships with no server and very little art, and every play is a share.
ideas.mainFix: Merged with Songbird and Music Box Mail into one 'little gifts by link' brand: several reveal styles, an optional tune, occasions, a keepsake drawer and abuse safeguards.
ideas.finalHook: Send a secret note. They have to iron it to read it.

market.fatalFlaw: It's a greeting-card toy: the recipient irons once for 15 seconds and leaves. Nothing brings the sender back until the next occasion. The 'dead-letter office' story needs a lot of writing.
market.returnPlay: Occasions (birthdays, Valentine's, 'open when you're sad'), reply chains, a keepsake drawer of every note you've received, and a short daily story letter.
market.firstFrame: A crumpled, coffee-stained paper ball. An iron glides over it, wrinkles hiss flat, and brown handwriting blooms: 'I never told you, but...'
market.competitors: E-cards (Jacquie Lawson runs a paid subscription business on cozy animated cards), Kind Words (anonymous letters), scratch-card apps, 'open when' letters. None makes the reveal tactile and personal.
fixes: Position it as a cozy e-card product for occasions: birthday, Valentine's, apology, thank-you, 'open when'. Occasions are the return loop.
Add a keepsake drawer: every note you've ironed is saved locally (and optionally to a free account) as a little box of letters you reread.
Turn the story mode into a 31-day 'advent' of dead letters that slowly tell one neighbourhood mystery. Ship it seasonally rather than as a daily treadmill.
Offer reveal variants (iron, candle, rubbing pencil, steam) as stationery unlocks.
Add a preset-phrase mode for kids and shy people, and keep user text in the URL only (no server, no moderation).
market.moneyPath: $3 stationery/supporter pack. Seasonal paper packs at $1-2. Test a $10-15/yr 'unlimited occasions' plan aimed at older card-senders (the e-card market proves people pay). Valentine's is the launch window.
market.sharperHook: Send a secret note. They have to iron it to read it.

build.hardestRisk: Not tech, abuse: the page renders arbitrary friend-written text on your domain, so it can carry bullying, crush-harassment or phishing text ('click this link') under your brand, and you have no server to report or block it.
build.needsServer: none. Deflate+base64url the note (cap ~200 chars) into the query string; the reveal is client-side. Optional later: a tiny edge function only to serve a per-link OG preview image ('Someone left you a crumpled note').
build.artLoad: low: photograph or scan 5-6 real crumpled papers (human-made, cheap), one iron sprite, a cat paw stamp. Use the creator's own handwriting as a font (avoid licence issues with commercial handwriting fonts).
build.mobileWebIssues: WebGL normal-map + heat-accumulation shader is light and runs in IABs. The finger hides the iron: offset the iron ~60px above the touch point. Disable page scroll/zoom on the paper (touch-action:none) or iOS will scroll while you iron. No vibration on iOS (navigator.vibrate is a no-op), so the hiss sound and steam particles must carry the feedback. Audio only after first touch.
build.privacySafety: Free text to known friends is the whole hook, so: strip/never linkify URLs, 200-char cap, a simple profanity/slur filter on compose, 'presets only' stationery mode surfaced by default, and the text never visible in the URL or link preview. Add a visible 'this note was written by a player, not Lemon Ink' footer. Keep a private-message framing (no public wall).
build.stage1MVP: Write a note, get a link; the friend irons a crumpled page until the words bloom, then taps 'write back'.
build.portalFit: Portals can't do the link-to-friend loop (Playables bans network calls and outside sharing is awkward on Poki), so the portal SKU is the 'dead-letter office' story mode of authored notes: offline, fits Poki/CrazyGames/Playables. Discord Activity is plausible later (send a note to a channel member).
fixes: Cut the dead-letter story for Stage 1; ship compose -> link -> iron -> reply in a week.
Launch a Halloween 'invisible ink spell' paper now (Oct) and a Valentine's pack in Feb 2027.
Add 'reply chain' so a note link shows the earlier notes as a small stack (still URL-only, cap 3 deep).
Record real iron hiss and paper crinkle ASMR; the sound is the clip.
Supporter pack = stationery/inks/seals only; never paywall sending.

ideas.title: Tumbler
ideas.hook: Collect ugly beach rocks. Tumble them for real hours. Open the lid.
ideas.oneLiner: Walk a daily tideline picking up rough stones, load them into a rumbling rock tumbler that runs in a background tab, and days later open it to find what they became.
ideas.fantasy: Beachcomber and pebble collector with a shed of jars
ideas.coreLoop: Pick 5 rough stones from today's tideline (read the clues: weight, banding, a glint), choose the grit stage, let it tumble in real time with ASMR rumble, then pour out and rinse the batch to reveal polished stones for your shelf of open-odds series.
ideas.howItSpreads: Rock-tumbler reveals are an existing TikTok genre: the clip is the muddy pour then the rinse. Share card: 'My tumble #41: 1 moonstone, 1 secret fossil'. Daily shared tideline means everyone compares the same rocks.
ideas.monetization: Free with one tumbler; $3 unlock for a second and third barrel, a display cabinet, and jewellery-making (set stones into rings for your mascots); seasonal tidelines. Odds always shown, nothing sold randomly.
ideas.whatsNew: Real-time grinding stages as an idle loop with a genuine skill layer (reading rough stones, choosing when to move grit). The long wait makes the reveal earned, not bought.
ideas.closestExisting: No rock-tumbler game found (only physical kits). Nearest: geode-cracking hypercasual games and Grow a Garden mutations; this has multi-day anticipation and a knowledge skill.
ideas.buildNotes: Stones are procedural (noise-based banding, colour palettes, lustre shader), so art is minimal: a hand-drawn tumbler, a tideline backdrop, a shelf. Background-tab timing via timestamps. Sound design is the main craft investment.
cultureSignals: Blind boxes, Pop Mart and Labubu
Unboxing / mystery-reveal as a content format
ideas.verdictA: Rock-tumbler reveal is a proven TikTok genre, but sharing is a bolted-on card.
ideas.verdictB: Real tumbler wait gives an earned reveal and return reason; sharing is only a result card.

ideas.title: Lint Buddies
ideas.hook: Shave the fuzz off old sweaters. Felt the fuzz into tiny friends.
ideas.oneLiner: De-pill bobbly sweaters with a buzzing fabric shaver; the lint chamber fills with colourful fluff that you needle-felt into small plush creatures whose look depends on the sweaters you shaved.
ideas.fantasy: Neighbourhood knitwear rescuer with a felting habit
ideas.coreLoop: Neighbours drop off pilled sweaters; glide the shaver to pop off every bobble (CleanTok satisfaction plus a % clean score), empty the lint tin, then poke the fluff into a creature where colour mixes from your shaved sweaters decide which of 6+1 buddies forms.
ideas.howItSpreads: Two satisfying clips in one: the pill-shaving swipe and the fluff-to-plush felting reveal. 'First felted' tags for rare colour mixes; share card shows the buddy plus the sweaters it came from.
ideas.monetization: Free base series; $3 supporter pack for new sweater patterns (Fair Isle, Christmas jumper), a second felting series and a buddy display windowsill. No paid randomness: buddy outcome is a known recipe you can discover.
ideas.whatsNew: Turns waste (lint) from one satisfying verb into material for a creative second verb; collection is earned by recipe discovery, not chance.
ideas.closestExisting: No lint-shaver game found; nearest are hypercasual 'clean the clothes' games and Little Alchemy. Difference: two-stage verb chain and the plush outcome.
ideas.buildNotes: Pills are particles on a knit texture; shaving is a brush mask. Felting is a metaball blob that sharpens with each poke. Bespoke art: 7 simple chibi buddies, ~10 sweater textures (can be procedurally knit patterns). Small and shippable.
cultureSignals: 'Grandma hobbies' and the analog crafting revival
Blind boxes, Pop Mart and Labubu
ideas.verdictA: Shaving clip is great, but the two-stage verb chain blurs the 5-second hook.
ideas.verdictB: Two satisfying verbs, but the chain takes explaining and nothing about it travels by itself.

ideas.title: Kiln Day
ideas.hook: Glaze your pots, close the kiln, and wait for the opening.
ideas.oneLiner: Dip, pour and layer glazes on simple pots, load the kiln, and open it the next morning to discover how the layers ran, crackled and pooled; record new combinations in a shared glaze book.
ideas.fantasy: Potter in a small community studio
ideas.coreLoop: Choose a pot, layer 1-3 glazes with dips and pours (thickness and order matter), place it in the kiln by hot spot, fire overnight (or fast-fire), then open the kiln to reveal results and log discoveries.
ideas.howItSpreads: 'Kiln opening' is a beloved pottery TikTok/IG format; the clip is the door opening on a shelf of surprises. Global glaze book credits 'first discovered by' for combos. Share a pot as a link others can view and copy the recipe from.
ideas.monetization: Free base glazes; $4 supporter pack with extra glaze families (celadon, tenmoku, shino), a wood-fired kiln with ash effects, and studio decoration. Optional printed 'glaze tile' merch later.
ideas.whatsNew: Emergent combination discovery (Infinite Craft style) expressed as visual material science with a timed reveal, rather than word merging.
ideas.closestExisting: No glaze-discovery game found (Double Fine's Kiln is an arena brawler). Nearest: Little Alchemy for discovery, pottery-wheel toys for making.
ideas.buildNotes: Glaze is a shader: layered colour with flow simulated as a vertical blur/drip map plus crackle and speckle noise; pots are lathe-generated meshes from a few profiles. Art needs: studio backdrop, kiln, UI. Highly systemic, low art.
cultureSignals: 'Grandma hobbies' and the analog crafting revival
Unboxing / mystery-reveal as a content format
ideas.verdictA: Kiln-opening reveal is lovely; glaze shader must look real or the whole thing falls flat.
ideas.verdictB: Kiln opening is a proven reveal and glaze discovery has depth; the shader must look gorgeous or it fails.

ideas.title: Ear & Crumb
ideas.hook: Score the dough with one slash. Watch it bloom in the oven.
ideas.oneLiner: Draw cuts on a sourdough loaf with a razor, then watch a time-lapse bake where your cuts burst open into an ear, a wheat stalk or a happy accident; your sourdough starter is a little pet that needs feeding.
ideas.fantasy: Village baker at 5am
ideas.coreLoop: Feed your starter, shape the loaf, draw your scoring pattern with depth and angle, then bake: the oven-spring simulation opens your cuts in real time and the loaf is judged by the queue of neighbours who buy it.
ideas.howItSpreads: Bread-scoring is a huge IG/TikTok genre; the oven time-lapse of the cut opening is a perfect 8-second clip. Daily pattern challenge ('today: wheat') with a % match share card. Starter age is a gentle streak ('my starter Doughris is 40 days old').
ideas.monetization: Free; $3 bakery pack with more flours (rye, beetroot, charcoal), banneton flour stencils, an oven upgrade and bakery decor. Seasonal patterns (pumpkin loaf in October).
ideas.whatsNew: Draw-then-physics-reveal: you commit a line and a simulation decides the bloom, so the clip has suspense. The starter-as-pet supplies the soft daily ritual.
ideas.closestExisting: No bread-scoring game found. Nearest: draw-to-solve puzzles and cookie decorating games; Tamagotchi for the starter.
ideas.buildNotes: Loaf is a 2.5D heightfield; cuts are curves whose edges peel outward driven by an inflation sim and crust colouring by depth. One hand-drawn bakery, a starter jar with a face, a cat. Physics tuning is the main work and AI coding handles it well.
cultureSignals: Romanticize your life, slow living, quiet life
ideas.verdictA: Scoring bloom is a great clip; spread relies on a share card; physics tuning is real work.
ideas.verdictB: Scoring bloom is a lovely clip; after a dozen loaves the loop risks feeling samey.

ideas.title: Postmark
ideas.hook: Send a postcard to a friend. It arrives covered in strangers' stamps.
ideas.oneLiner: Write a postcard, seal it with wax and drop it in the box; it travels through other players' tiny post offices, each stamping it with their hand-carved mark, before reaching your friend days later.
ideas.fantasy: Postmaster of a tiny village post office in a world-wide slow-mail network
ideas.coreLoop: Each session a sack of real players' postcards arrives at your office; sort them by destination, stamp each with your carved stamp (satisfying thunk, ink pressure) and wax-seal your own outgoing card, then see where your sent cards have travelled.
ideas.howItSpreads: A friend gets a link: 'a postcard is on its way to you' with a live map of its route; the arrival is a reveal of all the stamps it gathered. Carving your own stamp (mirror-image) is a mini-creation people post. Clips: wax seal pour and press.
ideas.monetization: Free; $3 supporter pack for more stamp shapes, ink colours, wax colours, postcard illustrations by the creator, and a special 'express' route that still never skips the strangers.
ideas.whatsNew: Players are the network: each card's route is user-made content, and the slow travel turns messaging into a cozy anticipation ritual with a third-place feel.
ideas.closestExisting: Slowly (pen-pal app) and Kind Words (anonymous letters). Difference: it is a handled object; strangers touch it with play, and you know the recipient.
ideas.buildNotes: Needs a small backend (cards queue, routing). Use preset phrases plus free text only to known friends to avoid moderation. Stamp carving is a pixel editor with mirror preview. Art: postcard fronts (a few hand-drawn), office scene, wax shader.
cultureSignals: Loneliness epidemic and the search for low-cost third places
ideas.verdictA: Charming network, but routing backend, cold start and days-long latency weigh it down.
ideas.verdictB: Charming network idea, but needs critical mass, routing backend and moderation before it feels alive.

ideas.title: Snip & Unfold
ideas.hook: Fold the paper, make your cuts, unfold. Did you match today's pattern?
ideas.oneLiner: A daily paper-cutting puzzle: you see a target lace pattern (snowflake, window flower, lantern), fold the paper and snip so that unfolding it matches.
ideas.fantasy: Paper-cutter preparing window decorations for every house on the street
ideas.coreLoop: Study the target, choose folds (half, quarter, sixth), draw cuts on the folded wedge, unfold with a satisfying paper-rustle reveal, and score the match; each solved pattern goes up in a neighbour's window.
ideas.howItSpreads: Unfolding is a top-tier reveal clip. Daily puzzle with spoiler-free share ('3 folds, 4 cuts, 97% match' as a little grid). Free mode exports your design as a printable cut-out people actually make at home.
ideas.monetization: Free daily; $3 for the archive, a free-create mode with printing, and seasonal sets (Lunar New Year jianzhi, Christmas snowflakes, Diwali rangoli-inspired).
ideas.whatsNew: Reverse-engineering a symmetric pattern via cuts on folded paper is a spatial puzzle few games use; snowflake makers are toys with no goal.
ideas.closestExisting: Paper snowflake toys (Make-a-Flake), Paper 2: Origami Refolded and 'fold and one cut' puzzles. Difference: cuts plus fold symmetry against a daily target, with a real-world printable.
ideas.buildNotes: Pure geometry: polygon clipping and mirrored transforms, no art beyond paper textures and a window street. Very cheap content: patterns are generated from solution cuts. Excellent for a solo build.
cultureSignals: Lunar New Year (Year of the Goat)
ideas.verdictA: Cheap, clean daily puzzle with unfold reveal; Wordle-shaped but a real spatial verb.
ideas.verdictB: Daily spatial puzzle with a top-tier unfold reveal and cheap procedural content; real staying power.

ideas.title: Temperature Scarf
ideas.hook: Knit one row a day. Today's weather picks the colour.
ideas.oneLiner: A one-minute daily ritual: knit a single row of a scarf whose colour comes from your town's real temperature today; over a year it becomes a picture of your weather.
ideas.fantasy: Knitter in a rocking chair keeping a weather diary
ideas.coreLoop: Open once a day, see the real temperature turn into a yarn colour, knit the row in a gentle tap-rhythm (click-clack ASMR), and watch the scarf grow; missing a day leaves a cosy 'forgot' stitch, never a punishment.
ideas.howItSpreads: Temperature blankets are a real knitting trend; the share is your scarf so far, and comparing cities (Oslo vs Lagos) is naturally viral. Year-end 'unroll your scarf' video. Friends can knit side by side and see each other's scarves.
ideas.monetization: Free; $3 for palettes, other projects (blanket, hat, cat jumper), mood rows (pick a colour for how you feel) and exporting a real knitting chart to make it in yarn.
ideas.whatsNew: Real-world data as the content, bounded to one minute a day by design. It is a habit tracker that looks like a craft object.
ideas.closestExisting: Real temperature-blanket trackers (spreadsheet/apps), Finch. Difference: playable tactile knitting and a beautiful shareable object rather than a chart.
ideas.buildNotes: Weather API by location (coarse, no login), procedural knit rendering, a hand-drawn chair and window. Very low art; strongest asset is sound. Ships as a tiny PWA.
cultureSignals: 'Grandma hobbies' and the analog crafting revival
Romanticize your life, slow living, quiet life
Digital detox, screen-time anxiety and 'brain rot' backlash
Cozy games for older adults / accessibility-first
ideas.verdictA: Real knitting trend, one minute a day, tiny build; daily clip weak, year-end payoff strong.
ideas.verdictB: Lovely ritual and trivial build, but one tap a day is thin and the daily clip is dull.

ideas.title: Bracelet Swap
ideas.hook: Knot a friendship bracelet. Send it. See everyone's on your wrist.
ideas.oneLiner: Tie real friendship-bracelet knots to make chevrons, hearts and letters, then send the bracelet to a friend as a link; your wrist shows every bracelet friends have sent you.
ideas.fantasy: Summer-camp friend and festival bracelet trader
ideas.coreLoop: Pick thread colours, tap forward/backward knots row by row (the pattern emerges from real bracelet rules), tighten each knot with a satisfying pull, then gift it; collect gifts on your wrist.
ideas.howItSpreads: Bracelet trading is an existing social ritual (Eras-tour wave). Every bracelet sent is an invitation link. Clips: the wrist stack and the pattern emerging. Group chats: 'make one for the group'.
ideas.monetization: Free; $3 pack for beads, letter beads, metallic threads, charms and more wrist slots; seasonal patterns. Optional real-world pattern printouts.
ideas.whatsNew: Uses the genuine knot grammar of friendship bracelets as a light pattern puzzle, and the gift is the distribution mechanic.
ideas.closestExisting: BraceletBook (pattern site) and kids' bracelet-maker apps. Difference: real knot logic plus a social wrist collection that grows through friends.
ideas.buildNotes: Pattern grid generation is simple algorithmic logic; threads are coloured curves. Art: a wrist, a few hand illustrations, charms. Bracelets stored in the URL.
cultureSignals: Loneliness epidemic and the search for low-cost third places
'Grandma hobbies' and the analog crafting revival
Character IP crossing into cozy games
ideas.verdictA: Gift-as-invite works, but bracelet makers exist; knot grammar may confuse casual players.
ideas.verdictB: The gift is the distribution and the knot grammar is real; bracelet makers exist and loop is shallow.

ideas.title: Chime Porch
ideas.hook: Cut tubes, tune your wind chime, and hang it where the breeze plays it.
ideas.oneLiner: Saw metal and bamboo tubes to length to tune a wind chime, hang it on your porch, and let the wind play it; share your porch as a link that plays itself.
ideas.fantasy: Porch-sitter and amateur chime-maker on a windy hill street
ideas.coreLoop: Take a request ('a chime that sounds like rain'), cut tubes (shorter = higher), test-tap, adjust, hang; the breeze plays it while you sit, and neighbours' porches along the street play their own.
ideas.howItSpreads: The share is a sound: a link that opens your porch playing in the wind (perfect for study/sleep). Ambient YouTube 'porch with chimes in the rain' long videos. Clip: tuning a tube until it rings right.
ideas.monetization: Free; $3 for materials (glass, shell, ceramic), weather (rain, snow, thunder far away), a second porch and longer ambient sessions/focus timer.
ideas.whatsNew: An instrument-building game where the wind is the performer: sound design is the content, and it becomes an ambient companion.
ideas.closestExisting: No chime-tuning game found; nearest are Incredibox/Sprunki (music making) and ambient sound mixers. Difference: physical tuning verb and generative wind performance.
ideas.buildNotes: Procedural audio (modal synthesis via WebAudio) means zero sound assets beyond reverb. Art: one porch scene with day/night palette swaps, a few tube materials. Very solo-friendly.
cultureSignals: Something cozy to run while working (desktop companions)
ideas.verdictA: Sound-first idea on silent-scrolling phones; better ambient companion than viral clip.
ideas.verdictB: Procedural sound is cheap and novel, but muted phone clips and a crowded ambient lane hurt it.

ideas.title: Big Fluff
ideas.hook: Bath the soggy dog, blow-dry it, and watch it become enormous.
ideas.oneLiner: Run a tiny pet salon where every wet, skinny-looking animal gets towelled and blow-dried into an absurd ball of fluff; brush and style, then hand them back to delighted owners.
ideas.fantasy: Pet groomer on a quiet high street
ideas.coreLoop: Towel the drip off, sweep the dryer to expand the fur volume (each strand-cluster puffs with physics), brush into a style, then the before/after photo goes in the salon window.
ideas.howItSpreads: Wet-pet vs dry-pet and groomer transformations are proven viral formats. Built-in before/after card. Daily 'today's customer' gets the same animal for everyone so styles can be compared.
ideas.monetization: Free; $3 pack with breeds (Samoyed, Pomeranian, Persian, sheep), bows, colours (pet-safe chalk), salon decor. Year of the Goat sheep event.
ideas.whatsNew: Volume as reward: the satisfying moment is size growth from drying, an inversion of cleaning games where things only get tidier.
ideas.closestExisting: Hypercasual pet salon games (wash/cut). Difference: fur volume simulation as the core spectacle, cozy pace, before/after sharing.
ideas.buildNotes: Fur as a 2D shell/strand-cluster field with a 'dampness' parameter controlling volume; feasible in WebGL. Art: 6 animals in a simple chibi style with two states, which is the main human art cost.
cultureSignals: Lunar New Year (Year of the Goat) + Steam Sheep Fest
ideas.verdictA: Wet-to-fluffy transformation clip is irresistible; fur sim and pet-salon genre overlap hold it back.
ideas.verdictB: Fluff-explosion clip sells instantly; underneath it's a pet-salon hypercasual with thin repeat play.

ideas.title: Leaf Pile
ideas.hook: Rake the biggest leaf pile on the street. Then jump in.
ideas.oneLiner: Rake autumn leaves into a pile with satisfying swishes; when it is tall enough, you (or the dog) jump in and they explode everywhere, and you rake again.
ideas.fantasy: Autumn afternoon in a front garden with neighbours raking too
ideas.coreLoop: Rake leaves into a pile (piles slump if too steep), the pile height becomes your jump; jump to scatter them in a joyful burst that seeds new leaf colours and occasionally hidden things (acorns, a lost mitten, a sleeping hedgehog).
ideas.howItSpreads: Perfect October clip: the explosion of leaves. Share card: 'my pile: 1.4m, found a hedgehog'. Link-share lets friends rake the same garden in real time (a small co-op raking party).
ideas.monetization: Free; $2 for seasons (snow shovelling, cherry petals in spring, beach seaweed), new gardens and jumpers (cat, toddler, granddad).
ideas.whatsNew: A Sisyphean loop that is joyful: you build to destroy, and destruction is the reward that resets the toy.
ideas.closestExisting: Leaf-raking toy apps and Placid Plastic Duck-style idle toys. Difference: pile-height skill plus jump payoff and seasonal swap.
ideas.buildNotes: 2D particle leaves with a heightmap pile; very cheap. Art: a garden backdrop, 5 leaf shapes, a few jumpers. Could be a first-week jam release timed to October.
ideas.verdictA: Instant October toy; little staying power or money beyond the season.
ideas.verdictB: Great October clip, but a one-joke toy; the co-op raking is bolted on.

ideas.title: Pressed
ideas.hook: Arrange flowers, close the heavy book, open it a week later.
ideas.oneLiner: Lay real-shaped flowers and leaves on a page, close the flower press, and later open it to see how everything flattened, spread and overlapped into a pressed-flower card.
ideas.fantasy: Botanical archivist filling an old herbarium
ideas.coreLoop: Collect today's six flowers on a walk, arrange them (petals overlap and bend), close the press and wait (real time or quick press), then open to reveal the flattened art and file it in your herbarium or send it as a card.
ideas.howItSpreads: The open-the-book reveal is the clip. Daily same six flowers for everyone, gallery of everyone's pressings; send a pressed card link to a friend.
ideas.monetization: Free daily; $3 for regional flora packs, card stock, framing, and a herbarium export (printable PDF).
ideas.whatsNew: Arrangement with a deformation reveal: you cannot fully control the result, which makes each card personal and the reveal suspenseful.
ideas.closestExisting: Flower arranging games (e.g. Flower Shop sims) and Botany Manor. Difference: one-shot press transform and herbarium collection.
ideas.buildNotes: Flowers as layered 2D meshes that flatten/spread and blend translucency on press. Needs hand-drawn flower sprites (about 20 to start), which a botanical illustrator could supply; maybe scanned real pressed flowers (human-made, authentic).
cultureSignals: 'Grandma hobbies' and the analog crafting revival
Unboxing / mystery-reveal as a content format
ideas.verdictA: Pretty and cottagecore, but needs botanical art and the reveal is subtle on a phone.
ideas.verdictB: Pleasant press reveal, but needs real botanical art and the reveal is subtle on a phone.

ideas.title: Marbled
ideas.hook: Drip ink on water, comb it, lay the paper, lift.
ideas.oneLiner: Paper-marbling for a stationer's shop: float colours on size, rake them with combs into peacock and stone patterns, then lift a sheet to reveal the print that becomes book endpapers.
ideas.fantasy: Stationer and bookbinder in an old arcade
ideas.coreLoop: Drop inks, drag stylus and combs (fluid sim), lay the paper and lift for the reveal; customers order a mood ('a stormy sea for a pirate novel') and you bind it into a little book on the shelf.
ideas.howItSpreads: Marbling (ebru/suminagashi) is a proven 'oddly satisfying' genre; the lift is the clip. Prints export as phone wallpapers, which spreads the art with a watermark link.
ideas.monetization: Free; $3 for ink sets, combs, gold leaf, and high-res wallpaper export. Later: printed notebooks as merch.
ideas.whatsNew: A real fluid art craft as a gentle shop loop where each order is a mood prompt; output is a usable artifact (wallpaper).
ideas.closestExisting: Web marbling toys and fluid-paint apps. Difference: shop fantasy, orders, binding collection and the lift reveal.
ideas.buildNotes: WebGL fluid/advection sim (well documented, AI-friendly). Art: shop interior, book spines. Patterns are procedural, so art cost is tiny.
cultureSignals: 'Grandma hobbies' and the analog crafting revival
ideas.verdictA: Marbling lift is top-tier satisfying footage; fluid toys exist and the shop layer is thin.
ideas.verdictB: Marbling lift is ASMR gold, but marbling toys already exist and the shop wrapper adds little.

ideas.title: Wind-Up Parade
ideas.hook: Wind each toy just enough so they all reach the birthday cake.
ideas.oneLiner: In a toy-repair shop after closing, wind up clockwork toys by the exact number of turns so they waddle, bump and hop across the workbench into a happy parade.
ideas.fantasy: Night-time toy mender whose toys perform when the shop is dark
ideas.coreLoop: Each scene has toys and a goal (gather at the cake, ring the bell); twist each key a chosen number of clicks, release all together, and watch the chain of bumps and hops play out; tweak and replay.
ideas.howItSpreads: Chain-reaction clips with cute clockwork toys; near-misses for streamers. Level editor with shareable links for player-made puzzles.
ideas.monetization: Free 30 levels; $4 unlock for 100 more, the editor, and new toys (tin frog, mouse, robot, cat). Daily scene with clicks-used share.
ideas.whatsNew: Winding amount as the only input: a quantity-planning puzzle with no aiming, closer to choreography than to physics-shooting.
ideas.closestExisting: Incredible Machine-style contraption puzzles and Cut the Rope. Difference: one quantized input per toy and simultaneous release.
ideas.buildNotes: Deterministic 2D sim so solutions replay exactly; 8 toy sprites with simple walk cycles. Level generation can be assisted by a solver script.
cultureSignals: Character IP crossing into cozy games
ideas.verdictA: Solid premium puzzle, but a contraption-puzzle variant with weak cozy-player demand signal.
ideas.verdictB: Solid premium puzzle with an editor; not cozy-viral and level design is a real cost.

ideas.title: Two Pairs of Hands
ideas.hook: Chores that need two people. Send the link, grab a corner.
ideas.oneLiner: A couples/friends co-op of tiny two-person household tasks: folding a fitted sheet, pivoting a sofa up the stairs, hanging curtains, winding a skein while the other holds it.
ideas.fantasy: Moving into a first flat together
ideas.coreLoop: Each task is a 1-minute two-touch cloth or rigid-body challenge where both players drag their own corner on their own phone; succeed (or comically fail) and the flat fills up room by room.
ideas.howItSpreads: Couples co-op is an under-served lane; the link is the invite. 'Pivot!' sofa clips and fitted-sheet chaos are relatable comedy. Share card: 'We folded the fitted sheet in 3 tries'.
ideas.monetization: Free first room; $4 one-time unlock for the whole flat (for both players, Webfishing-style multiplier), plus seasonal chores (Christmas tree in the stand).
ideas.whatsNew: Physical two-person cooperation via separate phones, built around the most relatable domestic struggles rather than cooking orders.
ideas.closestExisting: Overcooked/Moving Out (chaotic, timed), It Takes Two. Difference: no timer, tiny tasks, two phones from a link, gentle comedy.
ideas.buildNotes: Needs real-time sync (WebRTC or a small relay) and a cloth sim for sheets; rigid bodies for furniture. Art: one flat in simple flat-colour style. Moderate complexity, still solo-scale.
cultureSignals: Loneliness epidemic and the search for low-cost third places
ideas.verdictA: Couples lane and link-native, but realtime sync plus cloth sim is heavy for solo.
ideas.verdictB: Couples co-op with relatable comedy, but realtime netcode plus cloth sim; contra-03 does it cheaper.

ideas.title: Flake Journal
ideas.hook: Catch snowflakes on your mitten. No two are alike. Name yours.
ideas.oneLiner: Stand out in a winter evening catching falling snowflakes on a dark mitten, examine each one under a magnifier before it melts, and sketch the rare ones into a field journal.
ideas.fantasy: Snowflake Bentley-style naturalist on a winter porch
ideas.coreLoop: Move the mitten to catch flakes, inspect the crystal (procedurally grown: plates, stellar dendrites, needles), file it before it melts; rare forms and the world's 'first sighting' get your name.
ideas.howItSpreads: Every flake is unique and procedurally generated, so 'I found this one, it is mine' is a natural share. Melting adds bittersweet clip tension. Winter seasonal event with weather from your real location.
ideas.monetization: Free; $3 for a better magnifier, journal styles, a framed print export of your flakes, and frost/ice-crystal expansions.
ideas.whatsNew: Collecting with true uniqueness rather than fixed sets: a crystal-growth simulation produces infinite, nameable collectibles.
ideas.closestExisting: Snowflake generator toys; Pokemon-like catching games. Difference: naturalist observation, ephemerality and genuine uniqueness.
ideas.buildNotes: Reiter-style hexagonal crystal growth runs in a shader; art is a mitten, a porch, a journal. Ship for December.
ideas.verdictA: Lovely seasonal toy; thin loop and little sharing reason beyond a screenshot.
ideas.verdictB: Infinite unique flakes is neat but seasonal and the collecting has no social pull.

ideas.title: One Long Peel
ideas.hook: Peel the apple in one unbroken strip. How long can you go?
ideas.oneLiner: Turn a fruit under the knife with a steady circular gesture to peel it in a single curl; the unbroken strip is your score and its shape is a little artwork.
ideas.fantasy: Kitchen table at grandma's, making pie on an autumn afternoon
ideas.coreLoop: Steady your thumb circle (too fast and the strip snaps, too thick and you waste fruit), finish the peel, then the apples go into a pie that fills the shelf; daily fruit (apple, orange, persimmon, pear).
ideas.howItSpreads: Draw-a-Perfect-Circle-style skill score ('my peel: 92cm, unbroken') with a satisfying long-curl clip. Folk tradition: toss the peel over your shoulder and it forms the first letter of your sweetheart's name, a funny built-in share.
ideas.monetization: Free; $2 for fruit packs, knives, pie recipes and a pencil-sharpening and wood-plane mode (same verb, new curls).
ideas.whatsNew: A single continuous-gesture skill toy with craft output and a folk-magic punchline.
ideas.closestExisting: Draw a Perfect Circle; hypercasual fruit-peel ASMR games. Difference: real peeling feedback, letter-toss tradition, pie collection.
ideas.buildNotes: A rotating fruit mesh with a strip extruded from the gesture; simple. Art: a kitchen table and five fruits. Fast to ship as an October filler.
cultureSignals: Instant start, no tutorial, one input
'One more go' short loop with a visible score
Cozy games for older adults / accessibility-first
ideas.verdictA: Draw-a-Perfect-Circle clone in apple form; fun one-off, weak staying power.
ideas.verdictB: Instant skill toy with a perfect % share, but a five-minute novelty with nothing to sell.

ideas.title: Visible Mending
ideas.hook: Patch your neighbours' holes with pretty stitches, then see them wear it.
ideas.oneLiner: Darn and sashiko-stitch the holes in neighbours' jumpers, jeans and tote bags; over the seasons you see them walking past your window wearing your repairs, which grow into personal patchwork stories.
ideas.fantasy: Street-corner mender who knows everyone's clothes
ideas.coreLoop: A garment arrives with a procedural hole; stitch a path that must cover it (darning weave or sashiko pattern) using a limited thread length, then the owner walks past wearing it, and comes back later with a new tear on the same piece.
ideas.howItSpreads: Visible mending is a growing craft movement; before/after hole-to-patch clip. Shareable 'this jumper has 7 of my repairs' cards. Players can send a damaged garment link to a friend to mend.
ideas.monetization: Free; $3 for thread colours, sashiko pattern books, embroidery patches and a street of extra neighbours.
ideas.whatsNew: Persistent garments that accumulate your history and a living street where your work is visible on people.
ideas.closestExisting: Quilt Porch on the brief list (assembly, not repair), embroidery apps, Unpacking (story through objects). Difference: repair with constraints and garments that come back.
ideas.buildNotes: Stitch path is a line puzzle on a grid; hole coverage is a mask check. Art: 8 neighbours walking cycle (simple), garment textures. Writing is short vignettes.
cultureSignals: 'Grandma hobbies' and the analog crafting revival
Build a cast, not just a game
Cozy games that are NOT farming sims
ideas.verdictA: Heartfelt craft with persistent garments; slow hook and writing-heavy street.
ideas.verdictB: Warm persistent-garment idea, but slow-burn payoff that neither clips nor spreads well.

ideas.title: Last Sort Letterpress
ideas.hook: Set the poster in metal type. You only have three E's.
ideas.oneLiner: In a little letterpress shop, set townsfolk's posters and cards in backwards metal type with a limited case of letters, ink the forme and pull the print with a heavy, satisfying press.
ideas.fantasy: Village printer making lost-cat posters, wedding invitations and bake-sale signs
ideas.coreLoop: Read an order, compose the message within your case's limited letters (swap fonts, use ornaments, rephrase cleverly), lock it up, ink, and pull the press; the customer reacts to how charming and readable it is.
ideas.howItSpreads: Typography nerds and stationery TikTok; the press pull is ASMR gold. Create-a-print mode makes custom cards for friends as shareable links or printable PDFs. Daily 'make this message with this case' word puzzle with a score.
ideas.monetization: Free; $3 for type families, coloured inks, paper stocks, and print-to-PDF; later physical print collabs.
ideas.whatsNew: A word puzzle born from a real physical constraint (limited sorts) inside a tactile craft, not a guessing game.
ideas.closestExisting: Letterpress simulators and typing games; word puzzles like Wordle (different: composition under scarcity). No direct match known.
ideas.buildNotes: Almost all typography: free open-licence fonts, paper textures and a press illustration. Logic is simple string/letter-inventory checks.
cultureSignals: Cozy games for older adults / accessibility-first
ideas.verdictA: Clever scarcity word puzzle, but niche and hard to sell in a silent clip.
ideas.verdictB: Clever constraint word puzzle, but 'backwards metal type' needs explaining and appeals to a niche.

ideas.title: Cuttings
ideas.hook: Grow a houseplant, snip a cutting, text it to a friend. It keeps growing.
ideas.oneLiner: A houseplant game where the only way to get new plants is a cutting sent by link, and every plant shows its family tree back through everyone who passed it on.
ideas.fantasy: Being the friend with the jungle apartment who hands out pothos cuttings in jam jars.
ideas.coreLoop: Water and turn your plants for a minute a day, snip a cutting when one is ready, send it as a link, and see its descendants spread across the lineage map.
ideas.howItSpreads: Each cutting is a unique link ('Dana sent you a cutting of Biscuit, generation 14'). Opening it roots the plant in a jar right away, with no login. Small mutations (variegation, pink stems, a heart-shaped leaf) only show up after a cutting has been passed on, so rare traits spread through group chats. The clip is a zoom-out from one leaf to a world map of the plant's family tree.
ideas.monetization: $3 'Greenhouse' supporter pack: more shelf space, hand-drawn pots, macramé hangers and a grow light. Every plant can also be had for free through gifting.
ideas.whatsNew: Gifting is the only way to get plants, and the plant's lineage is the content. Real plant swaps and propagation culture are the mechanic itself.
ideas.closestExisting: Plant Daddy (itch.io) lets you share seed codes that make copies. Cuttings adds per-generation mutations, a public lineage tree and rare traits you can only get by gifting. Prōpa tracks lineage for real plants but is not a game.
ideas.buildNotes: Plants are procedural L-systems, so a few hand-drawn leaf shapes, pots and textures cover thousands of plants. The backend is a tiny parent-ID tree on a serverless key-value store. It is very feasible solo.
ideas.verdictA: Gift-only plants with lineage and mutations; gardening fantasy plus native group-chat spread.
ideas.verdictB: Gifting is the only way to get plants, plus mutations and lineage: spread and collecting built in.
ideas.whySurvived: The strongest built-in growth loop: plants only spread when people send them.
ideas.mainFix: A free 'mother plant' cutting for every newcomer, lineage leaderboards, a visible rare-mutation table and a light server so plants don't vanish.
ideas.finalHook: This plant has lived in 4,000 phones. Here's your cutting.

market.fatalFlaw: Cold start: if gifting is the only way to get a plant, a stranger arriving from TikTok with no friend playing has nothing. Tending a plant for one minute a day is thin and overlaps with Sill on the existing list.
market.returnPlay: The plant grows in real time, cuttings become ready on a cadence, rare mutations appear only in descendants, and your lineage's size keeps growing on the map.
market.firstFrame: An extreme close-up of one heart-shaped pothos leaf, then a fast zoom out through a glowing family tree over a world map: '4,112 descendants'.
market.competitors: Plant Daddy (seed codes), Viridi (succulent tending), Grow a Garden (mutations hype), Neko Atsume. Your own Sill concept is the closest internal rival. No one makes the lineage the content.
fixes: Every visitor gets a free cutting from a public 'mother plant' (a creator-named lineage per video), so the cold start is solved and the creator's audience forms one giant visible tree.
Add per-lineage leaderboards ('Biscuit: generation 31, 12 countries'). Group chats will compete for whose plant spreads furthest.
Use a clear mutation table (variegated, pink stem, heart leaf, moon leaf...) with a 6+1 secret, visible as empty silhouettes.
Use lineage milestone reveals as the clip format ('your cutting now has 100 descendants') and email the player when it happens.
Merge or differentiate from Sill: make Cuttings the windowsill garden whose only acquisition channel is gifting.
market.moneyPath: $3 Greenhouse supporter pack (shelf space, hand-drawn pots, macrame, grow light). Seasonal pots. Later a mobile app with widgets. Every plant stays free via gifting.
market.sharperHook: This plant has lived in 4,000 phones. Here's your cutting.

build.hardestRisk: Persistence: a care game whose plants live in localStorage will silently die when iOS evicts storage after 7 idle days or when the player first opened it inside TikTok's browser. Second: cold start (no plants without a giver).
build.needsServer: light. Cloudflare Worker + D1/KV: plant {id, parentId, generation, traits, coarse region, preset nickname}. ~$0-5/month at small scale. Rate-limit cutting creation per device to stop bot-spam of lineages.
build.artLoad: low-medium: L-system plants from ~8 hand-drawn leaf shapes, 6 pots, 2 shelf backgrounds. The risk is procedural plants looking generic; hand-draw leaves at large size and use a painted texture.
build.mobileWebIssues: No notifications on web unless installed to home screen (iOS web push needs a home-screen install), so 'water daily' must be forgiving (plants never die, just droop). Store plant state on the server keyed by a secret id in the URL so any browser can resume.
build.privacySafety: Lineage 'world map' implies location: use opt-in country/region only, never GPS or city by default. Nicknames from a preset generator ('Mossy Otter'), no free text, so no moderation and safe for kids.
build.stage1MVP: Open the creator's 'Biscuit' cutting link, root it in a jar, care for it for a few days, snip and send cuttings, and see a generation counter plus a simple family tree.
build.portalFit: Poor for portals: the gift loop is outside them (Playables bans network calls; Poki allows servers only for multiplayer with a privacy statement). Best on own site; Discord Activity later (pass cuttings in a server).
fixes: Seed everything from one creator plant so the 'my pothos has 40,000 descendants' video writes itself.
Allow a free starter plant (a seed packet) for strangers with no friend to gift them, so the 'gifting only' rule doesn't bounce TikTok visitors.
Server-side plant state keyed by link; show 'bookmark your shelf link' on first save.
Mutations only on cuttings, shown on a spoiler-free share card.
Drop the world map for Stage 1; show a tree diagram with generation counts.

ideas.title: Pass the Blanket
ideas.hook: One crochet blanket travels the internet. Add a square, pass it on.
ideas.oneLiner: A chain-letter crochet blanket: you crochet one granny square, stitch it on and pass the link along, and the blanket keeps growing as it travels from friend to friend.
ideas.fantasy: Joining a crochet circle, the kind where grandma's friends each made a square for a baby blanket.
ideas.coreLoop: Open the blanket link, crochet a granny square round by round (tap the rhythm and pick yarn colours), stitch it on, then pass the link to one or two people.
ideas.howItSpreads: The link is the blanket, and you can't add to it without being sent it. When you finish, a 6-second clip zooms out from your square to the whole blanket, and a map shows how far it has travelled ('this blanket has visited 41 cities'). Creators can start their own blankets for their communities.
ideas.monetization: $3 Yarn Basket: speciality yarns (mohair fuzz, variegated, glow-in-the-dark), border patterns and a printable poster of the finished blanket. A real blanket printed on demand is possible later.
ideas.whatsNew: Gartic-style chain play turned into slow, cooperative craft. The artifact is shared and keeps growing, and the travel log tells its story.
ideas.closestExisting: The real 'What Were You Thinking' square-swap crochet game and community crochet-alongs (offline). The fishing in Pond Party is not a craft chain, and Quilt Porch is single-player storytelling. No web game found where a blanket travels from link to link.
ideas.buildNotes: Granny squares are procedural geometry made of stitch sprites. The yarn texture is one hand-drawn stitch sprite, tinted. The backend is an append-only list per blanket. It needs moderation for colour patterns only (no text), so the risk is low.
ideas.verdictA: Chain blanket is a great shared artifact; monetization and per-player depth are thin.
ideas.verdictB: Travelling blanket is a beautiful link chain; individual players contribute once and rarely return.

ideas.title: Regulars
ideas.hook: Be a regular at a tiny café. The barista knows your order.
ideas.oneLiner: You aren't the barista, you're the customer. Visit the same little café for one minute a day, and over weeks the staff and the other real regulars start to recognise you.
ideas.fantasy: The quiet warmth of being known somewhere: 'the usual?'
ideas.coreLoop: Drop in once a day, order (the barista starts to guess right), sit at your seat, and nod at the other real players who visit around the same time each day. Small friendships grow from showing up, never from talking.
ideas.howItSpreads: Clips of the moment the barista says 'the usual?' after 30 days. Shareable 'regular card' stamps show your seat, your order and who you nod to. A link lets you 'save a seat' for a friend at the same hour.
ideas.monetization: $4 'tip jar' supporter pack: your own mug on the hook, a seat cushion and a choice of café cat. The café itself is free forever.
ideas.whatsNew: It flips the café game. The fantasy is being a regular rather than running the shop, and social presence is limited to nods and time-of-day overlap, a third place with no chat to moderate.
ideas.closestExisting: No web game found built on being the customer. Coffee Talk is closest in mood (you listen as the barista). Cozy Campfire Club is social chat; Regulars has no chat and rewards routine.
ideas.buildNotes: One fixed hand-drawn café scene, a small cast of staff and simple customer silhouettes coloured by player choice. Presence is grouped by hour bucket, with no realtime netcode needed. It needs a strong illustrator for one scene, and that's it.
cultureSignals: bounded daily rituals and forgiving streaks
ideas.verdictA: Fresh customer-side third place, but payoff takes weeks and nothing happens on camera.
ideas.verdictB: Genuinely fresh flip, but the payoff takes 30 days and there is almost nothing to do.

ideas.title: Lamplit
ideas.hook: Every lit window is a real person studying right now. Light yours.
ideas.oneLiner: A huge night-time library where every glowing lamp is someone focusing at that moment. Start a focus block to light your desk and add to the view.
ideas.fantasy: The quiet library at midnight during exams: everyone working, nobody alone.
ideas.coreLoop: Choose a desk, write a three-word intention, and keep a 25-minute lamp lit. When the block ends, your desk gains a small trace (a mug ring, a pressed flower, a stacked book) and the whole floor softly 'clinks'.
ideas.howItSpreads: The clip is a slow pull-back from one lamp to thousands across the façade, at real-time scale. 'Study with me' and lofi channels can embed a live façade, and a link invites a friend to the desk next to yours.
ideas.monetization: $3 desk kits (lamp shades, plants, a sleeping cat on the desk) and a long-form 'live library' YouTube stream that also carries the link.
ideas.whatsNew: Body doubling made into a single collective image. Your contribution is visible light in a shared building rather than a private timer, and the building's growing traces turn focus time into a slow, shared decoration.
ideas.closestExisting: Forest (a private tree), Focusmate (video calls) and lofi streams (passive). Lamplit makes many people's focus visible as one shared, live scene that anyone can join from a link.
ideas.buildNotes: One façade illustration plus window and lamp sprites, rendered by count. The presence counter is a simple websocket or polled counter, so it is very solo-feasible. Desk traces come from a small hand-drawn sticker set.
cultureSignals: bounded daily rituals and forgiving streaks
ideas.verdictA: Body-doubling demand is real; needs crowd density to look alive and earns little.
ideas.verdictB: Body-doubling demand is real and build is easy; focus-room apps exist and money is weak.

ideas.title: Group Pet
ideas.hook: A little pet your group chat raises together. It needs all of you.
ideas.oneLiner: A Tamagotchi shared by a friend group or a couple through one link. It grows only on days when more than one of you visits, and if you forget it just naps.
ideas.fantasy: The friend group's shared dog, or a couple's first pet, without the vet bills.
ideas.coreLoop: Open the link, give the pet one small thing (a snack, a pat, a toy), see who else visited today, and on 'everyone came' days watch it learn a new trick or grow a feature.
ideas.howItSpreads: The pet only works when shared: 'join our pet' links in group chats. The pet's milestones (first word, new hat, 'met all 5 parents') become postable cards, and clips show a pet that learned a quirk from one friend's habits.
ideas.monetization: $3 'nursery' pack per pet: a bed, outfits and an extra pet species. Couples gift-buy it. No energy or streak paywalls; a nap replaces death.
ideas.whatsNew: The Tamagotchi revival made social: the need for several people is the growth mechanic, and neglect only leads to naps. It is a natural fit for couples and group chats, which the brief lists as an open lane.
ideas.closestExisting: Finch (a solo self-care pet with friend gifts), Tamagotchi Uni (online but individual) and Neko Atsume. In Group Pet the pet is owned jointly and grows on shared presence.
ideas.buildNotes: One creature with modular parts (ears, tails, patterns) drawn by hand once and recombined. The backend is a per-pet document storing visits. Optional Discord Activity port. Low art cost.
cultureSignals: bounded daily rituals and forgiving streaks
ideas.verdictA: Shared Tamagotchi for group chats/couples; obvious hook, sharing is required to play.
ideas.verdictB: Shared group-chat pet needs everyone to visit: spread is the mechanic and the hook is instant.

ideas.title: Blind Date Bookshop
ideas.hook: Wrap a book in brown paper, write three clues, and see who falls for it.
ideas.oneLiner: Run a tiny bookshop where every book is sold 'blind': you wrap real books in kraft paper with three handwritten clues, and friends guess or 'date' it from your link.
ideas.fantasy: Being the indie bookseller whose blind-date shelf everyone trusts.
ideas.coreLoop: Choose a book you love from the catalogue, wrap it (twine, stamp, sticker) and write three short clues. Share it, and see how many people guessed it or took it home, while you unwrap other people's parcels.
ideas.howItSpreads: The parcel link is the post: 'Grief. Lighthouse. Slow tea. Guess my book?' The unwrapping reveal makes a 5-second clip that suits BookTok. A daily 'house parcel' gives everyone the same puzzle, and the stats ('62% guessed') are spoiler-free.
ideas.monetization: $3 Stationery pack (wax seals, washi, fountain-pen fonts and stamp sets), plus affiliate links to bookshops (Bookshop.org) on reveals.
ideas.whatsNew: Players make the puzzles: book lovers write clues for each other. It is a social bookish ritual, not a quiz, and it copies a real bookshop tradition.
ideas.closestExisting: Real 'blind date with a book' shelves and book-guessing dailies such as Bookle, which are curated quizzes. Here friends create parcels for friends, and the wrapping is the craft.
ideas.buildNotes: Mostly typography and paper textures. It uses an open book catalogue API (Open Library) for autocomplete. Clue text needs a word filter or a choose-from-word-tiles mode for safety. Very low art cost.
ideas.verdictA: BookTok ritual with player-made puzzles; clue text needs moderation, niche audience.
ideas.verdictB: Players make the puzzles for BookTok; free-text clues need moderation and the loop is niche.

ideas.title: Whisk
ideas.hook: Whisk matcha with your finger. How perfect is your foam?
ideas.oneLiner: A one-gesture matcha ritual: zigzag your finger to whisk a bowl of matcha and get a foam score, then pour it into the day's drink for the café cast.
ideas.fantasy: The calm mastery of a tea ceremony, done well in 20 seconds.
ideas.coreLoop: Sift, add water and whisk with a fast W-shaped zigzag (ASMR chasen sound, foam builds in real time), get a 'microfoam %', then finish one daily drink: strawberry matcha, an iced cloud, a hojicha latte.
ideas.howItSpreads: The 'Draw a Perfect Circle' share: '94.2% foam 🍵'. The clip is a top-down whisk with crisp sound, and the bubbles visibly shrink into silky foam. A daily drink gives everyone the same challenge.
ideas.monetization: $3 Tea Cabinet: hand-thrown bowls by a real ceramicist (credited), seasonal drinks and whisk styles. A tea brand collaboration is possible later.
ideas.whatsNew: A skill-percentage format built on a sensory gesture rather than drawing. The physical feel of whisking is the hook, and the rhythm can be learned.
ideas.closestExisting: Draw a Perfect Circle (a % skill test) and latte-art mini-games in café sims. No standalone game found built on matcha whisking.
ideas.buildNotes: A particle or shader foam simulation scored on gesture frequency and amplitude, plus a few hand-drawn bowls. Sound design is the main craft, and real recorded whisking can be used. One week to a prototype.
cultureSignals: bounded daily rituals and forgiving streaks
ideas.verdictA: Crisp skill-% toy with ASMR; novelty without much reason to return.
ideas.verdictB: Crisp % skill toy with great sound; a one-sitting novelty like most gesture scores.

ideas.title: Leaf Pile
ideas.hook: Rake up a giant leaf pile. Then let the dog jump in.
ideas.oneLiner: An autumn ritual toy: rake thousands of physics leaves into a pile, then choose who jumps in (dog, cat, grandpa, you) for an explosive, slow-motion finish.
ideas.fantasy: Being eight years old in October.
ideas.coreLoop: Each day your tree drops a new batch, including one rare leaf from a '6 + 1 secret' colour series. Rake it into the tallest pile you can, then tap to jump and see a splash score and a replay.
ideas.howItSpreads: The jump is the clip: a slow-motion leaf explosion with a crunchy sound. The game exports a 5-second vertical replay. Pile height and rare leaves found give a spoiler-free share. Seasonal snow then spring petals keep it going all year.
ideas.monetization: $3 'Backyard' pack: more jumpers (capybara, ghost costume), trees (ginkgo, maple, birch) and a leaf-press album for the rare leaves.
ideas.whatsNew: It turns a universal autumn memory into a physics toy with a built-in replay clip. It suits fallcore launch timing (early October, now) better than any existing cozy genre.
ideas.closestExisting: Raking mini-games inside larger sims, and sandbox toys such as Sandspiel. No standalone web game found built around the leaf-pile jump.
ideas.buildNotes: A GPU particle sim of a few thousand leaves; the rake is a force brush. Art is about 10 hand-drawn leaf sprites plus a few jumper animations. Shipping before Halloween is realistic.
ideas.verdictA: Leaf-jump explosion with exported replay is perfect fallcore clip; seasonal and shallow.
ideas.verdictB: Stronger leaf-pile version (replay export, rare leaves), but still a seasonal one-joke toy.

ideas.title: Laundromat
ideas.hook: Fold strangers' laundry while the dryer spins. Learn their whole lives.
ideas.oneLiner: A late-night laundromat where each wash cycle is a focus timer, and between cycles you fold a neighbour's basket, piecing together who they are from their clothes.
ideas.fantasy: The meditative Sunday-reset fold, plus quiet nosiness about the neighbours.
ideas.coreLoop: Start a cycle (a real 25-minute timer, the drum turning in the background), then fold the finished basket with swipe gestures into neat Marie Kondo stacks. Each basket reveals a cast member's story in small details (a tiny sock, a wedding shirt, a grief cardigan).
ideas.howItSpreads: Folding clips work as CleanTok and ASMR content (fabric swish, a perfect stack). Each neighbour's story arc gets theory comments ('the man with only one sock'), and players share their 'neat stack' photos.
ideas.monetization: $4 to unlock the full building of neighbours (the first two are free), plus detergent-scent ambience and lofi tracks.
ideas.whatsNew: It combines a focus timer, satisfying folding and storytelling through objects in one place. The wait for the dryer becomes the reason the game is bounded.
ideas.closestExisting: Unpacking (story through objects) and Forest (timer). Laundromat combines folding verbs with a body-doubling timer and serialised neighbour stories.
ideas.buildNotes: Clothes are a few hand-drawn garment templates with procedural colours and patterns. Folding is 2D mesh flips along fold lines. Writing the neighbour stories is the human craft, about 10 short arcs. Moderate art.
ideas.verdictA: Folding plus neighbour stories is pleasant but busy; paid narrative is credible, spread weak.
ideas.verdictB: Folding plus object stories is pleasant, but three ideas glued together without a sharp hook.

ideas.title: Ephemera Post
ideas.hook: Every day a little envelope of paper scraps arrives. Make a journal page.
ideas.oneLiner: A junk-journal game: open the day's envelope of ephemera (stamps, ticket stubs, pressed flowers, washi), collage a page, and send a page to a pen pal.
ideas.fantasy: A beautiful analogue journal without the clutter and the cost of supplies.
ideas.coreLoop: Unbox today's envelope (each set is '6 + 1 secret' ephemera), tear, tape and layer it onto a page, then save it to your book or mail it to a friend as a link.
ideas.howItSpreads: The month-end flip-through: one tap exports a vertical page-flip video, the exact format of 'journal with me' TikTok. Mailed pages arrive as sealed envelopes with an unboxing moment, and pen-pal chains form.
ideas.monetization: $3 seasonal ephemera packs (direct sale, contents shown), artist-collaboration sticker sets, and a print-your-journal PDF.
ideas.whatsNew: The ending is a flip-through video built for the feed, the daily supplies arrive with an unboxing, and pages can be mailed between people. It is journaling as a social ritual rather than free-form decorating.
ideas.closestExisting: Journaling apps (Zinnia, Journal it!) and decorating games (Cozy Corner, Unpacking). Ephemera Post adds daily unboxed supplies, mailing pages and auto flip-through exports.
ideas.buildNotes: Ephemera can be largely procedural (generated stamps, typographic tickets, scanned real textures from public-domain archives). Torn edges come from a shader. A tear-and-tape physics feel is the work, and it is solo-friendly.
ideas.verdictA: Journal-with-me flip-through export is smart; junk-journal decorating is a crowded app space.
ideas.verdictB: Flip-through export fits journal TikTok; decorating freedom competes with real journaling apps.

ideas.title: Tiny Kitchen
ideas.hook: Cook a real breakfast on a stove the size of a coin.
ideas.oneLiner: Miniature cooking: use tweezers and a toothpick spatula to cook real recipes at 1:12 scale, crack a quail-sized egg and fry a pancake the size of a fingernail, for tiny guests.
ideas.fantasy: The 'Tiny Kitchen' video fantasy of real food, absurdly small, made with care.
ideas.coreLoop: Each day brings one real recipe (pancakes, onigiri, cocoa). Do 4–6 tactile steps with tweezers while a tea-light flame heats the pan, plate it on a button-sized dish and serve a tiny guest (a mouse, a beetle, a sleepy kitten).
ideas.howItSpreads: The scale gag sells the clip: a giant hand-drawn finger next to a sizzling pancake, with sizzle ASMR. A shareable miniature 'menu card' of dishes cooked, and a daily dish everyone makes.
ideas.monetization: $4 Pantry: more recipe sets (Lunar New Year dumplings, Christmas pudding), tiny cookware and guests. A seasonal recipe pack every month.
ideas.whatsNew: Cooking games are about speed. This one is about scale and care, with no timer, no customers queuing and each recipe a little ritual. It uses miniature culture rather than restaurant fantasy.
ideas.closestExisting: The real 'Tiny Kitchen' and Re-Ment miniature videos, and cooking portal games (Sushi Party, Cooking Mama). Those are speed or score games; this one is slow and focused on miniature ASMR.
ideas.buildNotes: 2.5D top-down with a few hand-painted props per recipe. Each recipe is a step script plus particle and shader effects for batter, sizzle and steam. Real recorded kitchen sounds. Moderate art, reusable cookware.
ideas.verdictA: Tiny Kitchen fantasy reads instantly; per-recipe art and steps make content expensive.
ideas.verdictB: Scale gag is cute, but art-heavy per recipe and nothing spreads beyond the clip.

ideas.title: Jingle Bag
ideas.hook: Hang little charms on your bag. Watch them jiggle as you walk.
ideas.oneLiner: A bag-charm toy: earn and hang plush and enamel charms on your tote, then take a little walk and watch them sway, bump and jingle with real physics.
ideas.fantasy: Labubu-on-the-bag maximalism, a whole charm wall without spending money on blind boxes.
ideas.coreLoop: Complete a tiny daily errand walk (bakery, park, station) to earn one charm from a visible '6 + 1 secret' series, rearrange your chains and loops, and see how the bag swings on the walk.
ideas.howItSpreads: A 5-second looping GIF of your bag swaying and clinking: a perfect vertical clip with sound. A 'bag check' link lets friends see your charms, and the secret charms are what people brag about.
ideas.monetization: Direct-sale charm series ($2 each, contents shown, no randomness for money), plus creator-collaboration charms. Real merch of the cast charms later.
ideas.whatsNew: The collection is dynamic: charms are physics objects you hear and see moving together, not items on a shelf. It is the bag-charm trend itself as a toy.
ideas.closestExisting: Treat Box (shelf collecting) and Pop Mart's own app. Neither has a physics bag where the collection performs. No web game found built on charm physics.
ideas.buildNotes: Verlet chains plus rigid charms, simple and fun to tune. Each charm is one hand-drawn sprite, and series of 7 are manageable monthly. The cast doubles as merch-ready IP.
ideas.verdictA: Bag-charm trend as a physics toy; direct-sale charms are clean money; collection drives return.
ideas.verdictB: Rides peak Labubu and direct-sale charms monetize; jiggling a bag gets old fast.

ideas.title: Cats Are Liquid
ideas.hook: Cats are liquid. Pour them into teacups, boxes and boots.
ideas.oneLiner: A gentle physics puzzle built on the 'cats are liquid' meme: tilt and tap soft-body cats so they ooze into every container in the room until every cat is sitting.
ideas.fantasy: Proving the meme true: a world where every box, bowl and sink becomes a cat bed.
ideas.coreLoop: Each room has cats and odd containers. Nudge, tilt and wake cats so they flow, squish and loaf into a spot. When every cat 'fits and sits', the room purrs and the camera pans over the result.
ideas.howItSpreads: Clips of a fat cat slowly pouring into a teacup are instant TikTok. A daily room with a 'fewest nudges' cat-face grid to share, and players share screenshots of absurd fits (a cat in a fishbowl, a cat in a slipper).
ideas.monetization: $3 for extra room packs (bathroom, bookshop, Japanese inn) and cat breeds and coats. Free daily room.
ideas.whatsNew: Soft-body cats are the physical medium, so filling space is the puzzle. That differs from Suika merging and from colour sorting.
ideas.closestExisting: 'Cats are liquid sort puzzle' (mobile colour-sort), Liquid Cat (a platformer) and a Japanese 'carry plump cats with a spoon' jam game. None is a cozy soft-body fill-the-room puzzle with daily rooms.
ideas.buildNotes: A 2D soft-body cat (a spring-mass blob plus a face sprite and tail) is the main tech risk, but well documented. Rooms are a single hand-drawn background each. Cats come from one rig with palette swaps.
cultureSignals: bounded daily rituals and forgiving streaks
ideas.verdictA: Cats-are-liquid meme as soft-body puzzle; cat demand plus instantly funny clips; soft-body risk.
ideas.verdictB: Meme-true premise with clips that make themselves and a real puzzle loop; soft-body is the risk.
ideas.whySurvived: The best clip in the run plus a daily room that gives a reason to return; a natural portal game.
ideas.mainFix: Renamed (the original name may be taken); each breed pours differently; daily rooms built from a shared prop library; a sandbox photo room.
ideas.finalHook: Cats are liquid. Prove it: pour this chonk into a teacup.

market.fatalFlaw: The soft-body cat has to feel great on a phone. If it is jittery or fiddly, the 'pour' fantasy dies in 10 seconds. Handmade rooms are a content treadmill for one person. The name 'Cats are Liquid' is already used by a Steam platformer series (Last Quarter Studios; verify), so it hurts search and needs a new title.
market.returnPlay: A daily room with a par of nudges and a shareable cat-face grid. A breed collection where each breed flows differently. A sandbox photo room to keep.
market.firstFrame: A huge orange cat sits above a tiny teacup. A finger nudges it and it slowly glorps in, ending in a perfect loaf with ears sticking out. No text needed.
market.competitors: Mobile 'cats are liquid' colour-sort puzzles, the Cats are Liquid Steam platformers, Suika and merge physics games, the Liquid Cat gashapon toys (which prove the merch appeal). None is a cozy fill-the-room soft-body puzzle, and the clip beats all of them.
fixes: Give each breed its own viscosity: kitten = water, Persian = honey, chonk = pudding, sphynx = jelly. Breeds become both the puzzle variety and a 6+1 secret collection.
Generate daily rooms from a shared prop library (about 40 containers) with a solver-checked par, so one person isn't hand-making a room every day.
Add a no-goal 'Sandbox Loaf' mode: pour any cat into any prop and take a photo-mode screenshot. Players will make the clips for you.
Add a 'fits & sits' reveal pan with a purr sound that builds as the room fills. That is the ASMR hook.
Rename it something ownable and searchable, e.g. 'Loaf' or 'Pour Cat'. Keep 'cats are liquid' in the caption, not the title.
Ship the first build to Poki/CrazyGames early, since cat physics puzzles suit portals.
market.moneyPath: Free daily room. $3 one-time unlock for room packs (bathhouse, bookshop, Halloween attic) and coats. Portal ad revenue. Physical cat-in-cup stickers/acrylic standees. A $4-5 Steam/mobile premium with 100 rooms later.
market.sharperHook: Cats are liquid. Prove it: pour this chonk into a teacup.

build.hardestRisk: Tuning a soft-body cat that looks cute while squishing (not gross or jittery) and making 'fit every cat' a puzzle rather than a toy that's solved by shaking.
build.needsServer: none. Daily rooms can be pre-authored and bundled with a date index; score grid is client-side.
build.artLoad: medium: each room is a hand-drawn background plus container sprites; cats are one rig + palette swaps. Reduce by making containers modular props placed on 3 reusable room backdrops.
build.mobileWebIssues: Soft-body (pressure-spring blobs, ~24-32 nodes) x 5 cats is fine on phones if you cap physics at 60Hz with fixed steps. Device tilt (DeviceOrientation) needs an explicit permission tap on iOS, so default to drag/tap controls.
build.stage1MVP: Three rooms where you nudge 1-3 soft cats into cups, boxes and boots until they all sit, plus a share grid.
build.portalFit: Best portal fit of the set: single-player physics puzzle, offline, cute cats. Poki/CrazyGames and YouTube Playables (physics/puzzle is a top Playables category).
fixes: Prototype the cat body first for 2 days; if the squish isn't delightful, stop.
Score by 'cozy points' (how snugly each cat fits) not nudges, to keep it no-fail.
Daily room + streak with freezes; post a daily 'impossible fit' clip.
Avoid the existing 'cats are liquid' sort puzzle name collision in store search; pick a distinct title.

ideas.title: Unbothered
ideas.hook: Stack anything on a capybara's head. It does not care.
ideas.oneLiner: A hot-spring physics toy: balance ever more ridiculous things (a yuzu, a duckling, a teapot, a bicycle, another capybara) on a serene capybara, who just blinks when it all slides into the onsen.
ideas.fantasy: The capybara's state of being: completely calm while life piles up.
ideas.coreLoop: Each round, the onsen gives you a random sequence of objects. Place them on the capybara's head, and when the stack topples the capybara blinks, sighs and the items float around it. Score is height plus an 'unbothered' meter that only goes up.
ideas.howItSpreads: The escalation is the joke: 'I put a piano on him and he was fine'. Clips of the calm blink after chaos. A photo card of your tallest stack, and the daily object sequence is the same for everyone.
ideas.monetization: $3 Onsen pack: extra springs (snowy, cherry blossom, night lantern), object sets and capybara friends who join the bath (a cat, a monkey, a duck).
ideas.whatsNew: The failure screen is the cozy payoff: toppling is the calmest, funniest moment, not a loss. That turns the meme's 'unbothered' attitude into a no-fail rule.
ideas.closestExisting: Capybara Stack (May 2026) and Capybaradom Stack stack the capybaras themselves, and Creature Crash is a tabletop game. Unbothered stacks objects on one calm capybara in an onsen, and toppling is the reward, not a fail state. The market is crowded, so the charm must come from the calm reaction.
ideas.buildNotes: Matter.js or Box2D stacking. About 30 hand-drawn object sprites with simple collision shapes, and one capybara with a few blink and sigh frames. One week to a first playable.
ideas.verdictA: Capybara stacking market is already crowded; the calm blink is the only differentiator.
ideas.verdictB: Funny calm-blink payoff, but capybara stackers already crowd the market.

ideas.title: Thrift Bin
ideas.hook: Dig through today's thrift bin. Someone's going to find the treasure.
ideas.oneLiner: Everyone gets the same daily thrift bin. Dig through a physics pile of secondhand finds to spot the one real treasure (a 1970s teapot, a hand-knit cardigan) among the junk before your budget runs out.
ideas.fantasy: The thrill of the thrift find: 'you'll never believe what I got for $2'.
ideas.coreLoop: Shuffle, lift and flip items in a deep bin, inspect tags and maker's marks, spend your $10 on what you think is valuable, then reveal what each item was really worth and add the finds to your thrifted shelf.
ideas.howItSpreads: 'Thrift with me' and haul formats: a spoiler-free result card ('found the secret 🫖, spent $6.50'). Clips of the 'wait... is this?' reveal, and a shared daily bin gives everyone the same conversation.
ideas.monetization: $3 Collector's pass: archive of past bins, a bigger display shelf and 'estate sale' weekend specials. Optionally sell real cast-themed stickers.
ideas.whatsNew: A daily treasure hunt built on sustainability and the vintage culture of finding things, using your eye for small details (tags, hallmarks, stitching) rather than reflexes.
ideas.closestExisting: Thrift-shop management sims, hidden-object games and Wordle-style dailies. Thrift Bin is a physics rummage with shared daily stock and appraisal reveals.
ideas.buildNotes: A 2D physics pile of about 40 items per day drawn from a hand-drawn library of about 150 objects, with procedural tags and marks. Value clues are data-driven, and daily seeds keep content cheap.
ideas.verdictA: Shared daily thrift dig with appraisal reveal; 150-object library is real art cost.
ideas.verdictB: Shared daily bin with appraisal reveals has GeoGuessr-like legs; needs a large object library.

ideas.title: Golden Hour
ideas.hook: A game that only opens at your real sunset.
ideas.oneLiner: A tiny rooftop that unlocks only during your real local golden hour, where you take one photo a day of a procedural sky shaped by your actual weather, with a cast friend in the frame.
ideas.fantasy: The romanticise-your-life moment of stopping to watch the sunset, every day.
ideas.coreLoop: When your real sunset arrives, the rooftop opens. Arrange one friend and one prop, frame the live sky (clouds and colour driven by local weather data) and take the photo. Then the game closes until tomorrow.
ideas.howItSpreads: Its rule is the hook ('this game is only open for 40 minutes a day'). The daily postcard is shareable with a timestamp and location, and a world map shows sunsets moving west as players capture them.
ideas.monetization: $3 Camera Bag: film filters, frames, more rooftops (seaside, city, mountain hut) and a printable yearly calendar of your 365 sunsets.
ideas.whatsNew: Bounded play as a real-world constraint rather than a soft limit. Real weather and solar data make each day's sky unique to you, so the game turns into a daily habit of looking up.
ideas.closestExisting: 'golden hour' on itch.io (a photography sim, always available) and the Pokémon GO day/night cycle. No web game found that is only open at real sunset.
ideas.buildNotes: A shader sky driven by an open weather API plus a sunrise/sunset calculation. Cast and props are a few hand-drawn sprites. Very low content cost; the human craft is the sky palette design.
ideas.verdictA: 'Only open at your sunset' is a killer caption; the actual play is thin.
ideas.verdictB: The rule is a hook, but a 40-minute window shuts out most players and the loop is one photo.

ideas.title: Driftmail
