ideas.hook: Throw a bottle into the real ocean. A stranger finds it in days.
ideas.oneLiner: Draw a little picture, seal it in a bottle and throw it from your coast. It drifts along real ocean-current data and washes up on a stranger's beach days later.
ideas.fantasy: The romantic chance of a message reaching an unknown person far away.
ideas.coreLoop: Every day walk your beach and pick up whatever has washed in (bottles from real players, shells, sea glass), open the doodles, keep the ones you love on your shelf, then send one of your own.
ideas.howItSpreads: 'My bottle took 9 days from Lisbon to Brazil.' Clips of tracking a bottle across the map, and the doodle reveal is a little unboxing. Friends can throw bottles toward each other's coasts.
ideas.monetization: $3 Beachcomber pack: bottle glass colours, stamp seals, a larger shelf and a sea-glass collection book. The ocean gets an optional donation tie-in.
ideas.whatsNew: Real ocean physics makes delivery slow and uncertain, which is the emotional point. The connection with strangers uses doodles and stickers only (no text), which makes it safe for a third place.
ideas.closestExisting: Slowly (pen-pal app, text and real delays) and Floated (itch.io, a current-routing puzzle). Driftmail is a cozy beachcombing collection game with real drift data and a doodle-only exchange.
ideas.buildNotes: Uses public ocean surface current fields (NOAA OSCAR or similar) simplified into a coarse grid. Doodles are canvas strokes with a profanity and image-moderation queue or a sticker-only mode. Moderate backend; light art.
ideas.verdictA: Romantic bottle drift; stranger exchange needs moderation and cold-start volume.
ideas.verdictB: Real-current bottles are romantic; needs a stranger population and doodle moderation to work.

ideas.title: Advent Street
ideas.hook: A free advent calendar where every door is a tiny cozy game.
ideas.oneLiner: A 24-door December calendar where each door opens a 60-second cozy toy starring the cast, and each door opened worldwide lights a window on one shared snowy street.
ideas.fantasy: The childhood joy of the morning advent door, made for adults.
ideas.coreLoop: Open today's door (one per day, missed doors stay open to catch up), play its tiny toy (wrap a gift, ice a gingerbread, catch snowflakes), and see your window light up on the global street.
ideas.howItSpreads: A daily reveal in December, the cozy search peak. Clips of each day's door, a 'street' that visibly fills in as the world plays, and friends can share a house so their windows sit side by side.
ideas.monetization: $4 'Deluxe calendar' (bonus doors, a 25th-door finale gift, printable cast ornaments), and brands want advent-calendar collaborations. Can return each year.
ideas.whatsNew: A container format for 24 micro-toys rather than one game, built around the season's biggest ritual and advent-calendar culture (beauty and Lego advent). It doubles as a showcase for the whole cast.
ideas.closestExisting: Advent-calendar apps with one minigame or coupon per day, and Wordle-style dailies. Advent Street adds a collective street and a recurring cast, and each toy can become a seed for a future game.
ideas.buildNotes: 24 micro-toys sounds like a lot, but each is tiny and AI coding makes it fast. Art reuses the cast and one street illustration. Building must start in October to ship by December 1.
cultureSignals: bounded daily rituals and forgiving streaks
ideas.verdictA: Advent format is clear but 24 toys by December is a big, one-season build.
ideas.verdictB: Known advent format, one-month shelf life, and 24 toys by December is a heavy solo lift.

ideas.title: Soap Shavings
ideas.hook: Shave today's soap bar. Something cute is hiding inside.
ideas.oneLiner: Everyone in the world gets the same soap bar each day. Swipe to carve satisfying curls and reveal the hidden figure inside, part of a '6 + 1 secret' cast series.
ideas.fantasy: The soap-carving ASMR you watch at 1 a.m., done with your own finger.
ideas.coreLoop: Shave thin curls with swipe gestures (crisp ASMR), guess the shape of the figure from the silhouette, finish the reveal and put the figure on your bathroom shelf, which shows empty silhouettes for the ones you haven't found.
ideas.howItSpreads: The curls and the reveal are proven ASMR clips. A spoiler-free share of your guess and the number of swipes ('guessed it at 34% 🧼'). The daily secret figure creates 'did you get today's?' conversation.
ideas.monetization: $3 Bath Shelf: scented soap colours, layered marble bars and a whole carved figure collection book. Physical soap merch later.
ideas.whatsNew: Adds a shared daily bar, guess-before-reveal and a collectible cast to soap-cutting ASMR, which otherwise exists only as one-off ad-supported apps.
ideas.closestExisting: Soap Slice: ASMR Cutting 3D and Soap Cutting (mobile, ad-driven, hidden figures). Soap Shavings is web, daily and shared, with an open-odds cast collection and a guessing layer.
ideas.buildNotes: Voxel or SDF carving in a WebGL shader; curls are particles. Figures are simple hand-sculpted low-poly cast models (also reused elsewhere). Sound is key. A medium tech challenge; light art.
ideas.verdictA: Soap-cutting ASMR apps already exist; daily share adds little originality.
ideas.verdictB: Soap-cutting ASMR is proven but already exists; daily shared bar is the only new layer.

ideas.title: Mochi for Mayor
ideas.hook: A cozy town is electing its mayor. Help your favourite mascot win.
ideas.oneLiner: A seasonal 'oshi' election for the creator's cast: each mascot has its own one-minute daily chore game, and every chore you play counts as a vote. Results come out at a big festival.
ideas.fantasy: Being part of your favourite character's fandom, like the Sanrio ranking, but you help them win by doing nice things.
ideas.coreLoop: Choose your oshi, play their tiny daily chore (Mochi bakes, Pip sorts mail, Bean waters the park), watch the town gradually show their campaign posters, then go to the results festival.
ideas.howItSpreads: Team identity ('I'm Team Bean 🫘') drives memes, fan art and rivalries. Daily leaderboards make clips, the festival results are a live event worth streaming, and each election launches a new season.
ideas.monetization: $3 'Campaign badge' supporter pins per character (cosmetic only, no extra votes) and merch of the winner. It also builds the whole studio's cast as IP.
ideas.whatsNew: Instead of one game per hit, a cast-ranking ritual connects the studio's games. The fandom drives retention, and each mascot's chore is a seed prototype the creator can test.
ideas.closestExisting: The Sanrio Character Ranking (real-world vote, not a game) and Splatfest (team events inside Splatoon). Mochi for Mayor is a standalone cozy election built around micro-games.
ideas.buildNotes: 6–8 micro-games of about a day each with AI coding. The cast must be drawn once with care; they are reused everywhere. The backend is a vote counter. Ideal as the studio's cross-promotional hub.
cultureSignals: bounded daily rituals and forgiving streaks
ideas.verdictA: Needs a cast fandom that does not exist yet; better as later studio hub.
ideas.verdictB: Needs a fandom that doesn't exist yet; a studio hub, not a launch game.

ideas.title: Snail Post
ideas.hook: Pack a tiny parcel, send the link. A snail delivers it. Slowly.
ideas.oneLiner: A gift-wrapping game where a snail carries your parcel to a friend in real time, and the wait is part of the gift.
ideas.fantasy: Sending a hand-wrapped care package to someone you miss, and getting one back.
ideas.coreLoop: Forage a few trinkets on a short daily garden walk, wrap them (paper, string, wax seal, a sticker-phrase), send the link, then watch the snail crawl toward your friend and unwrap whatever arrives on your mantelpiece.
ideas.howItSpreads: The link IS the gift: the friend opens a live tracking page ('your parcel is 63% across the lettuce patch') and later an ASMR unwrapping reveal, then sends one back. Unboxing clips work as Shorts, and in each video the creator 'mails' a parcel to viewers with a code word, so it works where Shorts links are not clickable.
ideas.monetization: Free. $3 stationery pack (wrapping papers, wax seals, stamp designs), seasonal stamp sheets. No paid express delivery, because the wait stays sacred.
ideas.whatsNew: The delay is the feature, and the gift needs no text: trinkets carry the meaning (a warm sock means 'thinking of you'). Unboxing culture turned into a two-person ritual.
ideas.closestExisting: Postcrossing (real postcards), the Slowly pen-pal app (delayed text letters), Animal Crossing letters. Snail Post has no free text, makes the unboxing the payoff, and is link-native on the web.
ideas.buildNotes: No server needed: parcel contents, send time and route seed go in a compressed URL, and arrival is computed on the client. Art: about 40 trinkets, 10 papers, and a snail with 6 animations. No moderation needed because messages are only preset sticker phrases.
cultureSignals: Unboxing / mystery-reveal as a content format
Romanticize your life, slow living, quiet life
Loneliness epidemic and the search for low-cost third places
ideas.verdictA: Sweet slow-gift loop, serverless; weaker hook than its Snail Mail twin.
ideas.verdictB: Gift-and-wait with no server is lovely; overlaps contra-01, whose absurd snail hook is sharper.

ideas.title: Stone Soup
ideas.hook: Each friend adds one secret ingredient. Nobody knows what the soup becomes.
ideas.oneLiner: A pass-it-on cooking chain in which a pot travels through the group chat and turns into a named dish nobody planned.
ideas.fantasy: The folktale village where everyone's small contribution makes a feast.
ideas.coreLoop: Open the pot link, see only its colour, steam and the last ingredient, add one ingredient from your pantry, stir, and pass the link on. After six cooks, the last person serves it and a dish card reveals the full recipe, a generated name and Grandma's taste review.
ideas.howItSpreads: The chain runs through group chats, and hidden information keeps each link interesting. The final card ('Foggy Harbour Chowder, with a Sock') is a funny, shareable artifact. The creator starts a viewers' pot in each video and reveals the soup days later.
ideas.monetization: Free. $3 pantry pack (extra ingredients, ladles, pot skins); seasonal ingredient drops (pumpkin, chestnut, mochi).
ideas.whatsNew: A blind relay that builds one shared object. Like Gartic Phone, but with no drawing skill needed and no moderation, and the emergent result is a dish rather than a garbled picture.
ideas.closestExisting: Gartic Phone (drawing telephone chains), Little Alchemy (combinations). Stone Soup is async through links, builds one evolving object, and uses no drawing or text.
ideas.buildNotes: The URL holds the ingredient list (under 40 bytes), so no server is needed. A handwritten naming grammar plus flavour vectors makes the dish names emergent. Art: about 60 ingredient icons, a pot and Grandma's reactions. Optional global 'soup of the day' relay later.
cultureSignals: Build a cast, not just a game
Unboxing / mystery-reveal as a content format
ideas.verdictA: Blind relay soup with funny dish reveal; serverless, group-chat native; light monetization.
ideas.verdictB: Blind relay with a funny dish reveal, serverless and moderation-free; good group-chat legs.

market.fatalFlaw: Six sequential hops through a group chat almost never finish: one friend who doesn't open the link kills the chain, and the payoff only arrives at the end. Each turn is a single tap, so it's thin.
market.returnPlay: None as pitched. Fixed version: a discovered-dish cookbook with 'first discovery' credit.
market.firstFrame: A bubbling cauldron, with a caption counting six hands dropping things in (a carrot, a moon, a sock), then a card slams down: 'Foggy Harbour Chowder, with a Sock. Grandma: 4/5.'
market.competitors: Gartic Phone (telephone chains), Infinite Craft and Little Alchemy (emergent named results), exquisite-corpse games. Infinite Craft owns 'funny generated names'.
fixes: Make it parallel, not serial: everyone in the chat adds to the same pot link at any time, and anyone can serve once 4+ ingredients are in or at a timer.
Show partial reveals at each add ('it smells... of the sea?') so every turn has a payoff.
Add a global cookbook of discovered dish names with 'first cooked by your group' credit, which gives Infinite-Craft-style collection and bragging.
Add a weekly viewers' pot started in a Short, with the reveal in the next Short. This is the creator's content engine.
Add Grandma as a recurring character with taste quirks, so reviews are a running joke.
market.moneyPath: Weak. $3 pantry pack and seasonal ingredients. Better as a Discord Activity or a free viral funnel than as a revenue game.
market.sharperHook: Your group chat makes one soup. Nobody knows what's in it.

build.hardestRisk: The relay dies or pays off for only one person: chains stall at cook 3, and without a server earlier cooks never see the finished soup.
build.needsServer: none for private pots (ingredient ids in URL, <40 bytes). Light (Worker + KV counters) for the creator's 'viewers' pot', where thousands add ingredients to one pot and the reveal is a weighted dish.
build.artLoad: medium: ~60 ingredient icons is the bulk; start with 24 and a few Grandma reaction poses. The naming grammar is writing, which is cheap but needs human wit.
build.mobileWebIssues: Few: plain DOM/canvas. Long URLs are fine. Link previews in iMessage/WhatsApp are static unless you add an edge OG-image function, which would show the pot colour and boost tap-through.
build.privacySafety: No free text, so low risk. If cook names are shown, use presets.
build.stage1MVP: A 3-cook pot passed by link in a group chat, with a dish card the last cook posts back to the chat.
build.portalFit: Weak for portals (the loop is the group chat). Discord Activity is the natural home later (a pot in a channel). Playables can't do relays.
fixes: Cut to 3-4 cooks and let any cook 'serve early'.
Make the final card the thing posted back to the same group chat, so everyone sees it.
Run the public viewers' pot as the main creator format (YouTube Shorts links aren't clickable, but 'comment an ingredient' works without links).
Add 'first time anyone made this dish' discovery tags to borrow the Infinite Craft pattern.

ideas.title: Viewers' Island
ideas.hook: Everyone watching votes on what our little island gets tomorrow.
ideas.oneLiner: One shared island, grown one hand-drawn tile a day by the creator's audience, where every Short is the game's next move.
ideas.fantasy: Being a neighbour in a small seaside village you all built together.
ideas.coreLoop: Open today's island, walk it and find yesterday's addition, then vote between three hand-drawn options for tomorrow (a bakery, a bench by the cliff, a lighthouse cat); the winner gets built overnight.
ideas.howItSpreads: The creator's daily Short is the update: a timelapse reveal of the winning tile with the vote split. Viewers can vote in comments, which the creator counts as a bonus, so it works without clickable links. 'Day 100 of letting my viewers build an island' is a proven series format.
ideas.monetization: $4 'Keepsake' that forks the island into your own offline sandbox to keep decorating; supporter badge (a preset villager who appears in the town); printed island map posters later.
ideas.whatsNew: The creator's feed is the game's turn log. It is slow, curated, community-as-one-player play: one move a day, the reverse of chaotic Twitch Plays.
ideas.closestExisting: r/place and Twitch Plays Pokémon (fast, chaotic, open input), Townscaper (solo). Viewers' Island is daily, curated, cozy and led by video.
ideas.buildNotes: Tiny server: vote counters in edge KV plus one daily job. Content comes from the creator drawing about 3 tiles a day, which doubles as the video content. No moderation because choices are preset. The risk is the daily art treadmill, so batch-draw a few weeks ahead.
cultureSignals: Build in public and the creator's own audience
ideas.verdictA: Only works with an existing audience; daily art treadmill is the bottleneck.
ideas.verdictB: Depends on an audience the creator doesn't yet have, plus a daily art treadmill.

ideas.title: Bottled Weather
ideas.hook: Catch today's real weather in a jar and mail it to a friend far away.
ideas.oneLiner: Real local weather becomes a collectible you trade with friends in other cities, and their weather grows new flowers in your garden.
ideas.fantasy: Sending your grandmother in Lisbon a jar of your first snow.
ideas.coreLoop: Each day the game reads your real local weather, you catch it in a jar (tap raindrops, net fog, scoop snowflakes), send it to someone, and uncork jars they send you so your little garden grows weather-specific flowers and your shelf fills with labelled jars from around the world.
ideas.howItSpreads: 'Send me your snow' comment chains; people actively seek friends in other climates (a Sydney summer to a London December). The creator asks viewers from 30 countries to fill a jar shelf on camera. First-snow and monsoon moments are natural seasonal spikes.
ideas.monetization: $3 jar and label pack (shapes, corks, hand-lettered labels), collector's world map, printable jar-shelf poster.
ideas.whatsNew: Real weather becomes a tradeable good between people, so geographic difference is the value. Most real-weather games only mirror your own sky.
ideas.closestExisting: Weather Bottle (iOS: your own weather as a diorama), Pixel Weather Forecast (local weather buffs). Neither turns weather into gifts or a collection built across friendships.
ideas.buildNotes: The Open-Meteo free API needs no key; location is city-level only. The link holds the weather snapshot, city and date, with an optional HMAC from one edge function to stop spoofing. Art: about 12 weather jar types and about 30 weather flowers. No text, so no moderation.
cultureSignals: Romanticize your life, slow living, quiet life
Kidult collecting (adults buying toys for themselves)
ideas.verdictA: Weather as a tradeable gift is fresh; value depends on having far-away friends.
ideas.verdictB: Weather as a tradeable good is fresh, but needs friends in other climates to pay off.

ideas.title: Songbird
ideas.hook: Whistle a tune. A unique little bird hatches from it.
ideas.oneLiner: Your hum or whistle becomes a one-of-a-kind bird that sings your tune back, and friends whistle replies so the birds duet.
ideas.fantasy: Calling a bird down to your windowsill with a song only you know.
ideas.coreLoop: Whistle or hum for 3 seconds, watch an egg hatch a bird shaped by your melody (range sets the body, key sets the colours, rhythm sets the tail), send its link, and collect the birds friends whistle back onto a branch where pairs sing duets.
ideas.howItSpreads: Whistling on camera suits duets and stitches ('whistle back to my bird'). Reactions to absurd birds (someone hums a meme song) make good clips, and the bird link plays the tune on open.
ideas.monetization: $3 aviary pack (branches, nests, rare feather palettes), printable bird card with notation.
ideas.whatsNew: Your voice is the creature generator, and the reply mechanic turns a share into a duet. Mic toys usually make you imitate preset calls.
ideas.closestExisting: Nestling and Summoning Song (imitate predefined birdsong to attract birds). In Songbird you author the bird, and it travels by link.
ideas.buildNotes: Pitch detection by autocorrelation on the client. Only about 40 pitch values go in the URL, with no audio upload, so no moderation and no server. Art: about 30 modular hand-drawn bird parts. A phone mic-permission prompt adds one tap.
ideas.verdictA: Whistle-to-bird is a new verb with built-in duet replies; strong stitch/duet format.
ideas.verdictB: New verb: your whistle hatches a bird, and replies make duets; mic permission and novelty decay are risks.
ideas.stageLabel: Merged into Lemon Ink (a tune or bird attached to a note)

market.fatalFlaw: Mic permission plus whistling in public is a double barrier for people scrolling on a phone, and many people can't whistle in tune. After making one bird and showing it once, there's no day 2.
market.returnPlay: None as pitched. Fixed version: a windowsill guestbook that friends' birds visit, plus daily song prompts.
market.firstFrame: Someone whistles the first notes of a famous tune into a phone. An egg wobbles, cracks, and a lopsided pink bird pops out and sings it back slightly wrong.
market.competitors: Nestling and Summoning Song (imitate preset calls), Google's Fly Fly Away (whistle control), Chrome Music Lab, Incredibox/Sprunki. Authoring a creature from your voice is new.
fixes: Add a tap-a-melody fallback (5 wooden keys) so it works silently on a bus and for non-whistlers.
Make your link a persistent windowsill page: friends' reply birds roost there and duet. The share becomes a guestbook you revisit.
Add a daily song prompt ('the song stuck in your head', 'a lullaby') with a shared public branch for that day.
Make your bird learn: each new tune you teach changes its plumage a little, so one bird grows over weeks instead of making many disposable ones.
Use a field-guide collection of body types reached by melodic features (range, rhythm, key) to encourage experimenting.
market.moneyPath: Thin. $3 aviary pack and printable bird card with notation. Best as a free viral top-of-funnel that points to the creator's paid games.
market.sharperHook: Hum any song. A bird hatches that sings it back.

build.hardestRisk: Microphone access: TikTok/Instagram in-app browsers are WKWebView (iOS) / Android WebView, so behaviour depends on the host app; getUserMedia only works if the host app implements the permission delegate, and many visitors from TikTok/Instagram will get no prompt or a silent failure. Humming also causes octave errors in autocorrelation pitch detection.
build.needsServer: none. ~40 quantized pitch values + rhythm in the URL; no audio is ever uploaded.
build.artLoad: medium: ~30 modular bird parts plus colourways. Keep it to 4 body shapes x 3 tails x palettes at launch.
build.mobileWebIssues: Mic needs HTTPS, a user gesture and a permission prompt; iOS asks again in many contexts. Bluetooth headphones switch to low-quality call audio when the mic opens. Playback must start on a tap ('tap the egg'), and needs navigator.audioSession.type='playback' (or the silent switch mutes it). Background noise in public breaks detection.
build.privacySafety: Audio is processed locally and discarded, which is good; say so on the permission pre-prompt. Kids will use it, and it collects no text or audio.
build.stage1MVP: Whistle 3 seconds (or tap a 5-note pad), hatch a bird, send the link; the friend taps the egg to hear it and whistles a reply.
build.portalFit: Poor: Playables/Discord mic use is unproven or blocked inside iframes; portals would get the tap-pad version only.
fixes: Ship a tap-melody pad as an equal input, not a fallback, so IAB users still hatch a bird.
Detect IABs and show a clear 'open in browser to whistle' bar.
Target whistling (near-pure sine, easy to detect) over humming; snap to pentatonic.
If mic conversion is poor in testing, fold the bird-hatching into Music Box Mail as a cosmetic layer.

ideas.title: Window Across the Street
ideas.hook: Your friends' windows light up when they're home tonight.
ideas.oneLiner: Your friend group shares a little apartment building, and opening the link in the evening turns your window on.
ideas.fantasy: Living across the street from all your friends again.
ideas.coreLoop: Decorate your one window (curtains, plants, a cat on the sill), open the link in the evening so your lamp glows for a few hours, see whose lights are on, and tap a window to send a preset wave (steam from a mug, a paper plane); the building gains details over weeks of evenings together.
ideas.howItSpreads: Group-chat links, especially for long-distance friends and couples. 'Our friend group's building after 100 nights' and the building lighting up window by window make good clips.
ideas.monetization: $3 building styles (Paris walk-up, Tokyo danchi, treehouse), window decor packs; a group supporter unlock covers everyone.
ideas.whatsNew: Ambient presence without messaging: you feel company through lights rather than chat. A collective object whose only input is showing up.
ideas.closestExisting: Cozy Corner (daily-theme rooms), Locket and BeReal widgets (photo presence), Animal Crossing visits. Window Across the Street needs no photos, no text and no real-time play.
ideas.buildNotes: Tiny KV per building (up to 12 windows: decor plus last-open time). Preset gestures only, so no moderation. Art: building facades plus about 80 decor pieces. Cheap and fast to ship.
cultureSignals: Loneliness epidemic and the search for low-cost third places
ideas.verdictA: Presence-only friend building fits loneliness signal; quiet clip, needs a group to start.
ideas.verdictB: Presence-only third place for long-distance friends; quiet clip but sticky in group chats.

ideas.title: Kitten Passport
ideas.hook: Foster a kitten for a day, then pass it to a friend.
ideas.oneLiner: A link-borne kitten moves from home to home, collecting keepsakes and passport stamps, until it settles with its forever person.
ideas.fantasy: Being part of a little rescue network that raises a kitten together.
ideas.coreLoop: A procedurally patterned kitten arrives by link; feed it, play, give it one keepsake it carries (a scarf, a bell), then pass it on. After 7 homes it grows up and settles with the 7th person, while every earlier foster can check a postcard of where it ended up.
ideas.howItSpreads: Every play ends in a share. 'My kitten visited 7 homes in 4 countries' scrapbooks are shareable, and the creator releases a 'litter' in each video, giving viewers a code word to claim one. If nobody takes the kitten it just naps at your place, so there is no chain-letter guilt.
ideas.monetization: $3 shelter supporter pack (collars, scrapbook print, rare coat patterns); possible charity event with a real shelter.
ideas.whatsNew: The pet moves through your social graph and the cozy act is letting go. The scrapbook of homes is the payoff, not the pet's stats.
ideas.closestExisting: PetPal 3DS homebrew (strangers feed your pet via a relay), Flat Stanley and the travelling gnome, Postcrossing. In Kitten Passport the pet itself travels and you only keep the memory.
ideas.buildNotes: Kitten state goes in the URL, plus a tiny KV for chain tracking (kitten id to hops and country-level stamps, no personal data). Art: modular kitten with procedural coats, about 30 keepsakes. Preset items only, so no moderation.
cultureSignals: Build a cast, not just a game
Loneliness epidemic and the search for low-cost third places
ideas.verdictA: Travelling kitten through your social graph; cats plus Flat Stanley, no guilt mechanic.
ideas.verdictB: Pet that travels your social graph; each player's part is brief, so return is weak.

ideas.title: Where's Mochi?
ideas.hook: Hide your cat somewhere in a cozy room. Dare friends to find it.
ideas.oneLiner: A hide-and-seek maker in which you tuck a squishy cat into a cluttered room and send the link as a challenge.
ideas.fantasy: The cat that is somehow inside the laundry basket again.
ideas.coreLoop: Arrange a cozy room, squish Mochi into a pose (loaf, curl, liquid-in-a-vase) and camouflage her, send the link, and friends tap to find her and share 'found Mochi in 3 taps'; plus one official daily hide.
ideas.howItSpreads: The creator's Shorts are hides: viewers search the frame and comment 'behind the kettle!', which works without clickable links and drives comments. Players' hides become group-chat challenges and spoiler-free tap counts.
ideas.monetization: $3 room packs (bookshop, greenhouse, Halloween attic), extra cats with their own squish physics.
ideas.whatsNew: The player makes the hidden-object puzzle and it travels as a dare, and the cat's squishy body-shapes are the camouflage mechanic.
ideas.closestExisting: Hidden Folks and Where's Waldo (authored scenes), 'find the cat' photo memes. Here players author the hides and share them as links.
ideas.buildNotes: The room is a seed plus prop placements in the URL, so no server. Art: about 120 household props and about 12 cat poses with pattern variants. No user text or images, so no moderation.
ideas.verdictA: Find-the-cat dares work as comment-bait Shorts without links; prop art load moderate.
ideas.verdictB: Players author find-the-cat dares and Shorts drive comments; UGC gives it real legs.

market.fatalFlaw: Player-made hides are either trivially easy or unfair, and building a room takes 5 minutes while finding takes 5 seconds. Hidden-object cat games are already a crowded mobile genre.
market.returnPlay: A daily official hide and your own room that persists and gets decorated. Fixed version: a hider reputation ('sneakiest hider' stats).
market.firstFrame: A cluttered warm kitchen frozen for 3 seconds with 'Mochi is in here.' Then a zoom onto the kettle spout, where a single grey tail is curled.
market.competitors: Hidden Folks, Where's My Cat? (mobile), Secret Paws: Cozy Apartments, the many 'Hidden Cats' mobile titles, 'find the cat' photo memes. The player-authored dare is the only real difference.
fixes: Reverse the scoring so the HIDER earns points: 'only 2 of 9 friends found her'. Making the hide is the fun part and the brag.
Measure difficulty automatically from the first 5 finders and badge it (easy/sneaky/legendary) so dares are calibrated.
Make Mochi's squish poses (liquid in a vase, loaf in a bread basket) the camouflage puzzle. Cross-promote with Cats Are Liquid using the same cat rig.
Make the Shorts series the main growth channel: one hide a day, with answers in pinned comments.
Make the room a real home you decorate over time, so hides are a by-product of decorating.
market.moneyPath: $3 room packs and extra cats with their own squish styles. Portal hidden-object audience. Possibly bundle with Cats Are Liquid as one cat-universe supporter pack.
market.sharperHook: I hid my cat in this room. Only 12% of people find her.

build.hardestRisk: Art scope and fairness: 120 props + 12 cat poses is weeks of drawing, and player-made hides will be either trivially obvious or impossible (fully occluded cats).
build.needsServer: none. ~40 props x (id, x, y, layer) ~ 200 bytes in the URL plus cat pose/position.
build.artLoad: high as pitched. Reduce: 1 room, ~40 props sharing a strict flat palette, 4 cat poses with colour patterns, layer depth used for camouflage instead of bespoke poses.
build.mobileWebIssues: Hidden-object on a phone needs pinch-zoom and pan inside a canvas while page zoom is disabled. Tap accuracy: generous hitboxes. Otherwise light.
build.privacySafety: No text or images, so it's safe for kids and needs no moderation.
build.stage1MVP: One cluttered room with a daily official hide and a 'hide Mochi for a friend' editor that outputs a link and a 'found in N taps' card.
build.portalFit: Official daily hides fit Poki/CrazyGames/Playables well (offline, bundled). Player hides stay on own site.
fixes: Enforce a minimum visible area (for example 15% of the cat) in the editor so every hide is fair.
Lead with creator Shorts 'find the cat' (works without clickable links, drives comments).
Expand rooms only after the format proves itself; each room is a paid pack.
Let props be reused and recoloured across rooms.

ideas.title: Knitted For You
ideas.hook: Your cat can only wear sweaters your friends knit for it.
ideas.oneLiner: A gift-only crafting game: you knit sweaters for other people's cats, and your own wardrobe fills only with friends' gifts.
ideas.fantasy: Getting a lumpy, lovingly hand-knit sweater from a friend.
ideas.coreLoop: Open a friend's 'knit for me' link, knit a sweater with a rhythmic tap-stitch minigame on a small colourwork grid, and send it back; their cat wears it tagged 'knit by Sam', and you post your own request link to get sweaters for your cat.
ideas.howItSpreads: The core rule forces sharing: you cannot dress your own cat. Request links in bios ('knit for my cat'), creators knitting for followers on camera, and cats modelling friends' sweaters.
ideas.monetization: $3 yarn pack (mohair fuzz, sparkle, variegated), seasonal patterns, holiday ugly-sweater pack.
ideas.whatsNew: You craft only for others, so your collection is a record of your friendships, and the gift economy is the mechanic rather than a bonus.
ideas.closestExisting: Picrew and dress-up makers, Animal Crossing custom designs. Neither stops you making for yourself, and neither makes each item a gift with a giver's name.
ideas.buildNotes: Pattern (16x12 grid, 6-colour palette) in the URL, so no server. Abuse is limited by a tiny grid, limited palette, private links and no public gallery. Art: cat base, sweater shapes, yarn textures, knitting sounds.
cultureSignals: 'Grandma hobbies' and the analog crafting revival (crochet, knitting, embroidery, junk journals)
ideas.verdictA: You can only dress your cat with friends' knits; rule forces sharing elegantly.
ideas.verdictB: You can't dress your own cat: forced gifting is a clever spread rule; knitting grid limits clips.

ideas.title: Porch Chores
ideas.hook: Shell peas together while you chat. That's it. That's the game.
ideas.oneLiner: A Discord Activity and group-call companion where everyone sits on a porch doing slow tactile chores while they talk.
ideas.fantasy: Summer evenings on grandma's porch, hands busy, everyone talking.
ideas.coreLoop: Join from a voice call, sit on the shared porch, do a soothing chore (shell peas, fold dumplings, string beans, wind yarn) into a communal bowl, and at the end the batch becomes a labelled jar on the group's pantry shelf that records hours spent together.
ideas.howItSpreads: Discord Activity discovery inside servers; the same link works as a second screen during FaceTime or Zoom; study-with-me and body-doubling videos; ASMR pea-pop clips.
ideas.monetization: Discord in-activity SKUs or a $3 web unlock for chore packs (Lunar New Year dumplings, autumn apple peeling) and porch themes.
ideas.whatsNew: A game designed to take half your attention so conversation is the main event. No score, only a pantry that records time together.
ideas.closestExisting: Discord Activities such as Putt Party and Chef Showdown (competitive), Unpacking (tactile, solo). Porch Chores is a non-competitive fidget built for talking.
ideas.buildNotes: Discord Embedded App SDK plus a small real-time room (one Durable Object or Websocket room per call), low bandwidth. No text, so no moderation. Art: about 10 assets per chore, porch backgrounds per season.
cultureSignals: 'Grandma hobbies' and the analog crafting revival (crochet, knitting, embroidery, junk journals)
Focus timers and body doubling ('study with me', Forest, lofi streams)
ideas.verdictA: Lovely talk-companion, but Discord gating and nothing to film.
ideas.verdictB: Half-attention Discord fidget is smart positioning, but nothing to clip and Discord gating.

ideas.title: Pocket Hometown
ideas.hook: Type your town. Get it back as a tiny cozy diorama to decorate.
ideas.oneLiner: Real street and building maps become a hand-painted miniature of any place you love, ready to garden, light and share.
ideas.fantasy: Holding the place you grew up in like a snow globe.
ideas.coreLoop: Pick a place, watch it assemble as a soft diorama from real map data, plant gardens, string lights, add cats and seasonal snow, then share the link so people from there can add one memory pin (preset icons such as 'best bakery' or 'first-date bench').
ideas.howItSpreads: A 'comment your town and I'll make it' series gives endless Shorts. Locals share their town in hometown groups, and diaspora nostalgia drives emotional comments.
ideas.monetization: $4 high-res print or postcard export, regional style kits (Nordic, Mediterranean, Japanese), seasonal decor; later a Steam version.
ideas.whatsNew: Real geography with cozy decorating. Real-map games are management sims, and cozy builders use made-up land.
ideas.closestExisting: Townscaper (procedural, not real places), OSM2World, City Bus Manager and NIMBY Rails (real maps, management). No cozy decorate-your-real-town toy turned up in searches.
ideas.buildNotes: Pre-built vector tiles (Protomaps PMTiles on static hosting) or cached Overpass queries, with the area capped at about 500 m. Procedural buildings use about 6 hand-made regional style kits. Privacy: discourage home-address focus, centre on town squares; pins are preset icons only. Medium build difficulty, cheap to host.
cultureSignals: Romanticize your life, slow living, quiet life
ideas.verdictA: 'Type your town, get a cozy diorama' plus comment-your-town series; procedural buildings are hard.
ideas.verdictB: 'Your town as a diorama' is instantly wanted, but real-map procedural dioramas are hard to make pretty.

market.fatalFlaw: Making arbitrary real OSM data look hand-painted and cozy is a hard procedural-art problem, and most towns will come out as grey boxes. Rural and non-Western areas have poor building data. The delight is a one-time 'oh, my town', and the decorating afterwards is generic.
market.returnPlay: Fixed version only: real local weather and clock lighting as an ambient companion, and seasons.
market.firstFrame: A finger types 'Ghent'. A paper-craft town square unfolds out of the map, lamps flicker on, snow starts falling.
market.competitors: Isometric NYC (Andy Coenen, viral free), OSM2World and osm-isometric maps, Townscaper/Tiny Glade (made-up land), Etsy city-map posters, Google Earth.
fixes: If kept: shrink scope to one square or street (about 100 m) as a snow globe, not a town.
Use the creator's hand-polished 'comment your town' Shorts as the product test before building a generator.
Add real local weather and time-of-day lighting so it becomes a desk companion of home.
Sell prints/posters as the main product rather than the game.
market.moneyPath: Actually the best money of the set (personalised prints and postcards at $10-25 via print-on-demand). But that's a print business, not a cozy game.
market.sharperHook: Comment your town. I'll make it a tiny snow globe.

build.hardestRisk: Turning arbitrary real map data into a charming hand-made diorama on a phone: data quality varies wildly (rural OSM is sparse), procedural buildings look generic, and 3D rendering of real footprints is heavy on low-end phones.
build.needsServer: light-to-heavy: a planet PMTiles file (~110-120GB) on R2 is cheap (about $1-2/month storage) but you must build and maintain the pipeline; public Overpass has usage limits; shared memory pins need a database plus moderation. ODbL attribution required.
build.artLoad: high: 6 regional style kits of buildings, roofs, trees and decor is a large human art job.
build.mobileWebIssues: Heavy WebGL plus tile fetching inside IABs; long first load kills TikTok traffic. Area cap helps but still a multi-MB first load.
build.privacySafety: Worst of the set: people will type their home street, and 'comment your town' videos plus memory pins tie real places to users (doxxing, kids revealing where they live).
build.stage1MVP: Even the smallest version (one pre-baked town to decorate) loses the hook, which is 'type your town'.
build.portalFit: Blocked on Playables (no external network calls); Poki requires an exemption for external requests. Poor.
fixes: Park it. If revived, make it a creator content series (you build viewers' towns offline and post them) rather than a player tool.
Or limit to a curated list of public town squares baked offline, with no pins.

ideas.title: Lantern River
ideas.hook: Float one paper lantern a day on a river shared by everyone.
ideas.oneLiner: A nightly ritual where you fold one lantern and set it on a river carrying thousands of strangers' lights.
ideas.fantasy: Standing at a lantern festival with the whole world.
ideas.coreLoop: Once a day, fold and paint a lantern from preset motifs and colours, set it on the water, drift along the night river tapping strangers' lanterns (each shows only a motif and a city), and come back tomorrow to see 'your lantern was seen by 312 people'.
ideas.howItSpreads: A 'seen by' counter brings people back. The live river works as a long ambient YouTube or lofi video, and festival spikes (Lunar New Year, Loi Krathong, Diwali, Obon) bring seasonal surges.
ideas.monetization: $3 paper and motif packs, festival lantern sets, supporter 'ambient mode' (fullscreen river, timer).
ideas.whatsNew: A one-a-day anonymous gesture, with no text, no likes and no ranking, that still feels like company.
ideas.closestExisting: Sky: Children of the Light candles, Journey's anonymous co-presence, r/place. Lantern River is one bounded daily act on a calm shared surface.
ideas.buildNotes: Very light writes (one record of about 32 bytes per user per day) in edge KV; clients render a recent sample of about 2,000 lanterns. Presets only, so no moderation. Art: lantern parts, river night scene and water shader.
cultureSignals: Loneliness epidemic and the search for low-cost third places
ideas.verdictA: Calm anonymous ritual; needs crowd volume and has weak money.
ideas.verdictB: Calm shared ritual, but one tap a day and anonymous lanterns don't drive sharing.

ideas.title: Music Box Mail
ideas.hook: Punch a tune into a tiny music box. Send it. They turn the crank.
ideas.oneLiner: Compose on a paper punch strip that always sounds pretty, then gift the music box as a link the friend cranks with a finger.
ideas.fantasy: Giving someone a handmade music box with a song only for them.
ideas.coreLoop: Punch holes on a pentatonic paper strip, choose a carved box and figurine, send the link, and the friend cranks it with a circular finger motion to set the tempo, then can punch a harmony strip and send the duet back.
ideas.howItSpreads: Music-box ASMR, recreated meme songs and birthday tunes as links. 'Add a harmony to my box' duet chains, and the crank gesture looks great in clips.
ideas.monetization: $3 box carvings, figurines and tine timbres (glass, wood, toy piano); printable real punch strips for DIY music boxes.
ideas.whatsNew: The composition is a physical gift object with a hand-cranked reveal, and the reply makes it a duet.
ideas.closestExisting: Chrome Music Lab Song Maker, Incredibox and Sprunki (sequencers). Music Box Mail is a gift object with crank tactility and reply harmony.
ideas.buildNotes: Web Audio with samples recorded from a real music box (human-made sound as a selling point). The strip goes in the URL, so no server or moderation. Art: about 8 boxes and figurines.
cultureSignals: Unboxing / mystery-reveal as a content format
ideas.verdictA: Music box as giftable link with crank reveal; meme songs and duets; cheap, serverless.
ideas.verdictB: Gift music box with crank reveal is lovely; sequencer toys exist and monetization is thin.
ideas.stageLabel: Cut: a free web tool already does this; the music box became a Lemon Ink add-on

market.fatalFlaw: Music Box Fun (bryanbraun.com) already lets anyone punch music-box strips on the web and share them by link for free, and Music Box Composer exists too. Composing is a skill barrier, so most gifts will sound like noise. The recipient cranks once and leaves.
market.firstFrame: A tiny wooden music box. A finger circles the crank and a pentatonic version of a meme song tinkles out while the paper strip scrolls.
market.competitors: Music Box Fun (free web, punch and share), Music Box Composer, Chrome Music Lab Song Maker, Incredibox/Sprunki.
fixes: Don't ship it standalone. Fold the music box into Lemon Ink as a gift add-on ('your note comes with a tune') with presets of public-domain tunes.
If kept: pre-punched tune library plus 'add one flourish', so nobody has to compose.
Combine with Songbird and Lemon Ink into one 'little gifts by link' brand with one shared keepsake drawer.
market.moneyPath: Only as a cosmetic inside another gift product ($1-3 timbres and boxes).
market.sharperHook: Turn the crank. Someone made this song just for you.

build.hardestRisk: Fun for non-musicians on a 6-inch screen, and novelty versus Chrome Music Lab Song Maker, which already shares tunes by link. The gift-object framing and crank must clearly beat a sequencer.
build.needsServer: none. A 15-note pentatonic x 32-64 step strip is a bitmask of ~60-120 bytes in the URL, plus box/figurine ids.
build.artLoad: low: 3 boxes + 3 figurines at launch (not 8), a paper strip, a crank. Most of the 'art' is sound: record a real music box comb and a toy piano (human-made selling point).
build.mobileWebIssues: Ideal for autoplay rules: the crank gesture IS the user gesture that unlocks Web Audio. Set navigator.audioSession.type='playback' (with a silent-loop fallback) or iPhones on silent will play nothing, which kills the reveal. Circular crank gesture needs touch-action:none. Sample decoding on low-end Android is fine for <20 short samples.
build.privacySafety: No text, no voice, so very low risk. Optional 'from' name should be preset or 12 chars, filtered. User-recreated copyrighted melodies live in user links (not hosted), but avoid featuring famous songs in your own videos.
build.stage1MVP: Punch a tune on a scrolling strip, pick a box, send the link; the friend cranks to play it and can punch a harmony and send it back.
build.portalFit: Good. Compose-and-play is offline, so it works on Poki, CrazyGames and Playables (sharing becomes a screenshot/recording, not a link). Discord Activity fits too (crank a box together in a call).
fixes: Give non-musicians 'melody stamps' (birthday, lullaby, shuffle-pretty) and a 'make it prettier' button that snaps to chords.
Lead the hook with the gift moment: the recipient sees a wrapped box, unwraps, then cranks.
Merge Songbird's best idea in as an optional 'hum it in' import later, after mic permission is proven.
Sell real printable punch strips that fit $10 DIY music boxes as the physical upsell.

ideas.title: Leaf Boat
ideas.hook: Place three pebbles, then watch your leaf drift down today's stream.
ideas.oneLiner: A daily seeded stream where you nudge the currents with three pebbles, then sit back and watch your leaf's gentle ride.
ideas.fantasy: Racing leaves under the bridge as a kid.
ideas.coreLoop: See today's stream (same for everyone), place up to three pebbles to bend the currents, release your leaf for a calm 40-second ride past ducks and little falls, then share a spoiler-free route squiggle and time.
ideas.howItSpreads: The creator posts their run every morning and the game includes the creator's ghost leaf ('beat my leaf'). Drift footage is soothing Shorts material, and a ghost link lets friends race your exact run.
ideas.monetization: $3 leaf collection pack (maple, ginkgo, paper boat, duckling) plus an archive of past streams; good fit for YouTube Playables revenue.
ideas.whatsNew: A plan-then-watch daily: you set the rocks, physics does the rest, so there is no fail and suspense comes from the calm watch. The creator is a ghost inside each daily.
ideas.closestExisting: Placid Plastic Duck Simulator (watch only), Wordle (daily share). Leaf Boat adds a small decision and a ghost race.
ideas.buildNotes: Precomputed 2D flow field per daily seed with deterministic simulation; a ghost is seed plus pebble positions (tiny). Art: stream tile kit and about 12 leaves, seasonal swaps. Static hosting only.
cultureSignals: Build in public and the creator's own audience
ideas.verdictA: Tidy daily with creator ghost; low stakes, low demand signal.
ideas.verdictB: Neat plan-then-watch daily with ghosts; low drama for clips and a modest hook.

ideas.title: Over the Phone
ideas.hook: Grandma reads the recipe. You cook it. Neither of you sees both.
ideas.oneLiner: A two-phone cooking game: one person holds Grandma's vague handwritten recipe, the other holds the kitchen, and you talk it through.
ideas.fantasy: Calling your grandma to learn the family dish.
ideas.coreLoop: One player opens the recipe card ('a handful, until it smells right'), the other opens the kitchen from the same link, you talk it through (on a call or the same couch), and Grandma judges the dish warmly; every result, even a disaster, becomes a new page in your family recipe book.
ideas.howItSpreads: Couples, long-distance friends and parent-child pairs make funny miscommunication clips ('make your mom play this'). The link must be sent to a second person to play, and the recipe-book page is shareable.
ideas.monetization: $3 grandma packs with regional dishes (nonna, lola, babcia, nai nai) written by real people; seasonal holiday recipes.
ideas.whatsNew: Asymmetric co-op made cozy: no timer, no explosions, and failure turns into family lore. It needs no networking because both phones derive from one seed.
ideas.closestExisting: Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes (asymmetric, stressful), Overcooked (chaotic). Over the Phone is gentle, about food and family, and runs on two phones from one link.
ideas.buildNotes: Both screens share a seed code, so judging is local and there is no server. Art: about 50 ingredients, 4 grandmas, recipe cards in real handwriting. Writing is the main human-made content. Fills the couples and non-Western open lanes.
cultureSignals: Build a cast, not just a game
Romanticize your life, slow living, quiet life
ideas.verdictA: Asymmetric gentle co-op for couples/families; 'make your mom play this' clips; writing is the work.
ideas.verdictB: Gentle asymmetric co-op that forces a second player; funny clips, but content is consumed fast.

market.fatalFlaw: It needs two people available at the same moment with a voice channel. The stranger watching the clip is alone. Each authored recipe is consumed once, so content burns faster than one writer can produce it.
market.returnPlay: As pitched, only the recipe book. Fixed version: a weekly 'Sunday call' recipe, plus your family adding its own recipes.
market.firstFrame: A split screen: left, a shaky handwritten card reads 'a good handful of flour, until it looks right'. Right, a confused partner holds a cup of flour over a bowl. Caption: 'make your mum play this'.
market.competitors: We Cookin' (itch, the same asymmetric recipe/kitchen setup), Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes, Overcooked, Home Cooked and 'Just Like Grandma Used to Make' (itch). The format is not new; the gentle family framing is.
fixes: Make the killer feature a template where you type YOUR grandma's real recipe in her words and it becomes a playable card for your family. User content does the writing, and it is shared only by private link.
Add a weekly 'Sunday call' official recipe with a shareable spoon rating, giving a soft ritual cadence.
Ship it as a Discord Activity (voice is already on), which removes the hardest friction.
Add a one-person 'voicemail' mode: the recipe is read by a recorded human grandma voice line, for solo play.
Let the family recipe book export as a printable PDF zine.
market.moneyPath: $3 grandma packs written by real people from many cultures. A $5 printable/printed family recipe book of your results and your own family recipes (strong gift around holidays). Discord Activity reach.
market.sharperHook: Call your mum. One of you has the recipe. One has the kitchen.

build.hardestRisk: Content and activation, not tech: each recipe must be hand-written so the vague-instruction conversation is funny not frustrating, and a lone TikTok viewer can't play at all without recruiting a second person right now.
build.needsServer: none. Both phones derive state from a seed in the link; role chosen on open; the kitchen phone judges locally. A Discord Activity version would need a light server for OAuth token exchange.
build.artLoad: medium-high: ~50 ingredients, 4 grandmas, handwritten recipe cards and regional dishes written by real people. Start with 1 grandma, 12 ingredients, 3 recipes.
build.mobileWebIssues: Playing during a phone call works (speaker on), but many will use a video call app that takes over the screen; same-couch is the realistic default. Small screens make a kitchen with many items fiddly; use big cards.
build.privacySafety: No data. Represent real cultures carefully: credit and pay the real people who write each grandma pack, avoid caricature.
build.stage1MVP: One grandma, three recipes: one person opens the vague recipe card, the other the kitchen, from the same link, and Grandma rates the result.
build.portalFit: Discord Activities is the best fit (players are already in a voice call). Poki/Playables can't do two-device play without a server; a single-device pass-and-play mode could work there.
fixes: Add a solo 'Grandma calls you' mode (her lines appear as voice-note text) so lone viewers get a taste, then 'call someone' to play properly.
Make the result page a recipe-book card worth posting, including disasters.
Lead marketing with couples and 'make your mom play this' clips.
Plan Discord Activity as Stage 3 target.

ideas.title: Friendship Starter
ideas.hook: A friend's link gives you a sourdough starter. Feed it, bake, pass it on.
ideas.oneLiner: A forgiving pet-blob sourdough starter that arrives with a family tree, bakes loaves with shareable crumb shots, and splits to new friends.
ideas.fantasy: Keeping a starter that has been in the family for generations.
ideas.coreLoop: Feed your starter daily (miss a day and it gets sleepy, but it never dies), bake by kneading in rhythm and timing the proof to get a procedural crumb cross-section, then split a jar to friends and watch your descendants grow on the family tree.
ideas.howItSpreads: Lineage stats ('6 generations from the creator's original, 2,341 descendants') and crumb shots to compare. The creator gives away starters by code word in Shorts, riding the Amish Friendship Bread tradition and sourdough TikTok.
ideas.monetization: $3 bakery pack (bannetons, scoring stencils, heritage flours), named heritage starters as cosmetic origin skins.
ideas.whatsNew: The pet is inherited, not bought or hatched: it spreads like a real starter, and global lineage is the bragging right.
ideas.closestExisting: Starter Bakery (itch.io), D'ough (Ludum Dare), Dough Globe hardware. None tracks lineage across people or passes the pet on by link.
ideas.buildNotes: Tiny KV lineage (id, parent, descendant counter); crumb uses procedural bubble packing. Art: blob starter with about 12 faces and about 20 loaf shapes. Soft streak with freezes and revival.
cultureSignals: Gamified self-care and habit companions (Finch, Pokémon Sleep, Tamagotchi revival)
ideas.verdictA: Lineage pet spreads well but overlaps Cuttings and Ear & Crumb.
ideas.verdictB: Lineage pet works, but it's Cuttings with bread; Cuttings has stronger mutation pull.

ideas.title: Frog Family Photo
ideas.hook: Make your friend group as frogs. Everyone poses in one photo.
ideas.oneLiner: A group-chat portrait studio: each friend builds a frog, picks a pose and spot, and the cat photographer snaps the polaroid when all are in.
ideas.fantasy: Your friend group's annual family portrait, but frogs.
ideas.coreLoop: Open the group link, build your frog from preset parts, choose a pose and a place on the bench, watch the photo fill as friends join, then the cat photographer counts down and the polaroid drops into the group album; reshoot each season in costumes.
ideas.howItSpreads: Group chats and 'our group as frogs' story posts. Seasonal reshoots (Halloween costumes, sweaters) bring the group back, and the creator shoots fan photos.
ideas.monetization: $2 costume and backdrop packs per season, printable polaroid set, annual album export.
ideas.whatsNew: An avatar maker made collective and async: the output is one group artifact, not a solo avatar.
ideas.closestExisting: Picrew (solo avatars), Bitmoji group scenes, Mii Plaza. Frog Family Photo assembles one shared photo from everyone through a link.
ideas.buildNotes: Tiny KV per photo (up to 12 slots of part ids); client renders the polaroid. Presets only, no moderation. Art: about 100 frog parts, 10 backdrops, cat photographer. Very fast first playable.
cultureSignals: Build a cast, not just a game
ideas.verdictA: Group-chat frog portrait is instant fun; Picrew-adjacent, art-parts heavy.
ideas.verdictB: Group-chat portrait is easy and shareable, but a Picrew-style one-off between seasons.

ideas.title: Leaflings
ideas.hook: Photograph a real leaf on your walk. It becomes a little guy.
ideas.oneLiner: Snap real leaves (later petals, shells, snowflakes) and they become shape-true critters that live in your herbarium village.
ideas.fantasy: Every walk outside fills a little village with new neighbours.
ideas.coreLoop: Take a walk, photograph a leaf on plain ground, watch its exact silhouette and colours turn into a critter with eyes and wobbly legs, add it to your herbarium village, and trade leaflings with friends by link.
ideas.howItSpreads: 'I turned leaves from my walk into little guys' is a ready-made Short; comments post their own. It is a touch-grass, digital-detox angle in perfect autumn timing, and every leafling is unique.
ideas.monetization: $3 herbarium pack (village decor, frames), printable sticker sheet of your own leaflings, seasonal 'specimen' kits (spring petals, summer shells).
ideas.whatsNew: The real outdoors is the content generator: no two players have the same creatures, and finding is physical, not a gacha.
ideas.closestExisting: Labo Leaves (arrange preset leaves into animals), Pokémon GO (real-world walking). In Leaflings, your own photographed leaf is the creature.
ideas.buildNotes: On-device segmentation (colour threshold plus contour on a plain background; optional small model); the photo never leaves the phone. The link stores a simplified polygon (about 60 points) and palette, so silhouettes only and no moderation. Art: eye, mouth and limb kits plus village. Static hosting.
cultureSignals: Digital detox, screen-time anxiety and 'brain rot' backlash
Kidult collecting (adults buying toys for themselves)
ideas.verdictA: 'My walk's leaves became little guys' is a native Short; segmentation is the risk.
ideas.verdictB: Real leaves become critters: a new verb, ideal autumn Shorts, outdoor content engine; segmentation is the risk.
ideas.whySurvived: Most original idea in the run; both critics ranked it near the top once it accepts any flat object and works from a photo.
ideas.mainFix: Accept any flat object, use the photo picker instead of a live camera, add a field guide and daily villager requests.
ideas.finalHook: Any leaf you find becomes a little guy. Bring him home.

market.fatalFlaw: The core verb needs you outdoors, with a camera, a leaf and a plain background. Most viewers are scrolling on a couch at night, so the clip sells something they can't do right now. It is also seasonal: in December there are no leaves.
market.returnPlay: Weak as pitched (only 'go for a walk'). Fixed version: a field-guide collection of leaf shapes and species, daily villager 'specimen requests' and seasonal object types.
market.firstFrame: A hand holds up a real red maple leaf on a pavement. Snap, and it peels off the photo, grows googly eyes and wobbly legs, and waddles into a little paper village.
market.competitors: Labo Leaves (preset leaves), Plum's Creaturizer (PBS Kids), Pikmin Bloom and Pokemon GO (walking), Seek/iNaturalist (identification). No one turns your own photographed object into a critter.
fixes: Accept any flat object, not just leaves: petals, ticket stubs, crisps, pasta, a sock. Then it works at home tonight and in winter. 'Leaf' stays the autumn launch skin.
Add a camera-roll import and a 'trace it with your finger' fallback, so no camera permission is needed to start.

Sort shapes into about 30 silhouette classes (oak, maple, ginkgo, heart, needle...). That gives a field guide with empty silhouette slots and a 6+1 secret per season: real collection pressure without a gacha.
Add daily villager requests ('the baker wants something red and pointy') so players have a reason to look at the ground tomorrow.
Make the trade link carry the critter so a friend can adopt it into their village. Leaves from other cities become exotic species.
Start with a free set of 6 'pressed starter leaves' so the very first session has creatures.
market.moneyPath: $3 herbarium pack (village decor, frames, extra shelves). $5-8 printed sticker sheet of YOUR own leaflings via print-on-demand (cozy, personal, non-predatory). A natural mobile app later, where camera games belong.
market.sharperHook: Any leaf you find becomes a little guy. Bring him home.

build.hardestRisk: Camera capture plus segmentation: TikTok/Instagram in-app browsers are WKWebView (iOS) / Android WebView, so behaviour depends on the host app; live getUserMedia is unreliable or absent there, and colour-threshold contouring fails on grass, pavement or shadows.
build.needsServer: none. The leaf becomes a ~60-point polygon + 3-colour palette (~250 bytes) in the trade link; the photo never leaves the phone.
build.artLoad: medium: an eye/mouth/limb kit (~20 pieces) plus a village. Keep the village to one hand-drawn herbarium page with slots, not a walkable town.
build.mobileWebIssues: Use <input type=file accept=image/*> (OS photo picker/camera sheet) instead of a live getUserMedia viewfinder; it works in Safari, Chrome and most IABs, though some iOS webviews misbehave with the camera option, so also offer the photo library. Collections live in localStorage, which iOS Safari can evict after 7 days of no visits and which is separate in TikTok's browser vs Safari, so players lose their village. Need an export/restore link.
build.privacySafety: Strip EXIF (GPS) by redrawing to canvas before processing; never upload photos. Kids are a likely audience, so keep trading link-only with no names/text beyond presets. Encourage 'leaf on paper' shots (no faces, no homes).
build.stage1MVP: Pick or snap a photo of a leaf on paper, watch it become a wobbly critter, and share its link or a sticker image.
build.portalFit: Weak for portals: Playables has no camera path and portal players are indoors; a portal version would need a 'draw your own leaf' mode. Good for own site/itch; TikTok Minis would need the native runtime (HTML Minis end Aug 2026).
fixes: Ship now: it's October and the 'leaves from my walk' clip is seasonal; delay misses the window.
Instruct 'put it on white paper' and add a manual 'trace with your finger' fallback when segmentation fails.
Add a 'draw a leaf' input so IAB users and portal players can still play.
Make the save a URL ('your herbarium link') and nudge 'Add to Home Screen' (home-screen web apps avoid Safari's 7-day eviction).
Detect TikTok/Instagram IABs and show a one-tap 'open in Safari/Chrome for the camera' bar.

ideas.title: The Feed That Ends
ideas.hook: A cozy For You page: thirty swipes of tiny chores, then it says goodnight.
ideas.oneLiner: A vertical-swipe feed of 3-second cozy microgames (pop a jam lid, tuck in a cat) that ends, today's feed being the same for everyone.
ideas.fantasy: A feed that leaves you calmer than it found you.
ideas.coreLoop: Swipe up through 30 micro-cards, each a tiny tactile act lasting a few seconds (water the fern, fold a towel, pet the cat), until the feed says 'that's enough for today' and gives a spoiler-free strip of your moments.
ideas.howItSpreads: Screen recordings look exactly like TikTok, so the clip reads natively in the feed and the satire is the caption. 'My feed today' posts and a daily cadence. It suits TikTok Minis and YouTube Playables.
ideas.monetization: $3 'evening feed' (a second calm feed at night), card packs; Playables and Minis revenue.
ideas.whatsNew: The doomscroll format turned against itself: bounded, tactile, kind. The game's form is the platform's own UI.
ideas.closestExisting: WarioWare (frantic microgames), Stimulation Clicker (overstimulation satire), Unpacking (tactile chores). The Feed That Ends is a calm, bounded feed format.
ideas.buildNotes: Microgame engine with about 50 cards remixed by a daily seed; static hosting. Art is moderate (one illustration per card), so start with 40 cards and add 3 a week as content. No server or moderation.
cultureSignals: Digital detox, screen-time anxiety and 'brain rot' backlash
Absurd escalation / premise as the hook
ideas.verdictA: Anti-doomscroll satire reads natively in feed; 50 illustrated cards is real content load.
ideas.verdictB: Satirical calm feed reads natively on TikTok; needs a steady stream of illustrated cards.

ideas.title: Sand Jar
ideas.hook: Each friend pours one layer of coloured sand a day. Watch your month stack.
ideas.oneLiner: A shared group-chat jar where everyone pours one tilt-controlled layer of mood-coloured sand a day, building a striped keepsake together.
ideas.fantasy: The sand-art bottles from the seaside, made with your people.
ideas.coreLoop: Open the jar link once a day, pick a colour for your day, tilt the phone to pour a layer that slumps and drifts realistically, see friends' layers above and below, and when the jar is full it gets corked and shelved as that month's keepsake.
ideas.howItSpreads: The pour is oddly satisfying ASMR footage, and finished striped jars look great. Group check-ins without words, especially for long-distance friends, and month-end jar reveals.
ideas.monetization: $3 jar shapes, glitter and glow sands, a printable 'year of jars' shelf poster.
ideas.whatsNew: Collective mood journaling as a physical, beautiful artifact: falling-sand physics used for a ritual, not a sandbox.
ideas.closestExisting: Sandspiel (falling-sand toy), Daylio (solo mood tracking), real sand-art bottles. Sand Jar is a shared, daily, wordless ritual.
ideas.buildNotes: Falling-sand sim on canvas or WebGL; state is a compact column-height and colour run-length per layer in tiny KV per jar. Mostly procedural art (jar, shelf, sand shaders). Colours only, so no moderation.
cultureSignals: Loneliness epidemic and the search for low-cost third places
Gamified self-care and habit companions (Finch, Pokémon Sleep, Tamagotchi revival)
ideas.verdictA: Shared mood sand jar is wordless, beautiful and group-native; money is light.
ideas.verdictB: Wordless group mood jar with a satisfying pour; lovely but low stakes per day.

ideas.title: Snail Mail
ideas.hook: Send your friend a letter by snail. An actual snail. It takes weeks.
ideas.oneLiner: Write a short note, hand it to a named snail, and it crawls toward your friend's city in real time at real snail speed (slightly sped up), with a shareable tracking link.
ideas.fantasy: Slow, devoted, absurd care: someone thought of you so much they trusted a snail with it.
ideas.coreLoop: Check in on your snails each day, feed them a leaf to pick a scenic detour, collect postcards from the towns they pass, and open snails arriving for you.
ideas.howItSpreads: The tracking link IS the invite: the recipient opens a page showing 'Gerald is 412 km away, currently resting under a dock in Lyon'. Clips: 'I sent my sister a letter by snail 3 weeks ago, it just crossed the border'. Arrival day is a reveal moment people film.
ideas.monetization: Free: one snail at a time. $3 supporter pack: a stable of 5 snails, shell paints, wax seals, a 'express slug' joke option that is somehow slower. Optional printed real postcard on arrival as a later physical upsell.
ideas.whatsNew: Inverts instant messaging into a game of anticipation; the slowness is the punchline and the gift. Real map data plus procedural roadside 'diary entries' produce endless content without bespoke art.
ideas.closestExisting: Slowly (pen-pal app with distance-based delay) and older snail-racing games; none make the courier a cute character you follow in real time with a public tracking link. Searches found no real-time snail-courier game.
ideas.buildNotes: Very feasible: map tiles (OpenStreetMap/Leaflet), great-circle path, server stores letters; city-level location only (player picks a city, never exact address). Art: 1 snail sprite with paintable shell, ~20 weather/rest vignettes, tiny town postcards drawn as simple line art. Moderation: letters only readable by recipient link holder.
cultureSignals: Unboxing / mystery-reveal as a content format
Loneliness epidemic and the search for low-cost third places
Absurd escalation / premise as the hook
ideas.verdictA: Absurd real-speed snail courier with live tracking link; caption sells itself.
ideas.verdictB: Absurd real-time snail courier with tracking link: the funniest slow-mail hook of the set.

market.fatalFlaw: The core is waiting, and the web has no push notifications. The sender forgets the snail by day 4, and the recipient never learns it arrived. At truly weeks-long timescales, the dot barely moves between visits.
market.returnPlay: Daily diary postcards from the snail's actual route. A leaf feed that picks a detour. Both sender and recipient can cheer the snail. The arrival ceremony.
market.firstFrame: A tracking map: 'Gerald: 412 km to go. Currently: napping under a dock in Lyon.' Cut to a snail with a tiny satchel and a 3-week counter.
market.competitors: Slowly (delayed pen-pal app), FutureMe (letters to the future), the Real Snail Mail art project, Neko Atsume / Placid Duck (check-in ambience). No one has a cute real-time courier with a public tracking page.
fixes: Cap trips at 3-10 days with 'snail-standard' speed. Weeks is the joke in the caption; days is the game.
Add an 'Add arrival to calendar' (.ics) button for the recipient, plus optional email. This solves the missing push notification.
Let the recipient also feed and cheer the snail. Two people checking in daily doubles retention and makes it relational.
Generate route postcards from real place data along the path (a bridge, a bakery, a river). Collect them in an album. This is the day-2 to day-20 content.
Seasonal event: 'Post by Dec 1 for Christmas Day delivery.' This one is huge for timing, and Valentine's works the same way.
Make the letter a sealed reveal (wax seal, unfolding) on arrival so people film the opening.
market.moneyPath: Free: one snail. $3 stable of 5 snails plus shell paints and seals. $6-10 optional real printed postcard of the journey map mailed to the recipient (a real-world upsell that fits the theme).
market.sharperHook: I sent my sister a letter by snail. It's in Lyon now.

build.hardestRisk: Retention over weeks with no web notifications: senders and recipients forget the snail, so the arrival payoff never happens. Plus map tiles: the public OpenStreetMap tile servers forbid heavy app use.
build.needsServer: none if done right: the link carries {send time, from city, to city, sealed note}; position is computed from the clock, so tracking is deterministic. Light only if you want a sender 'delivered!' callback.
build.artLoad: medium: snail + shell paints are cheap, but '20 vignettes' and postcards per town add up. Use a hand-drawn stylised map (one illustration) instead of OSM tiles, and procedural diary text.
build.mobileWebIssues: No push without home-screen install on iOS; offer an 'add arrival to calendar' .ics download (no server). Storage eviction means the sender's outbox can vanish; the tracking link itself must be the save.
build.privacySafety: City-level only, chosen from a list (never GPS). A free-text letter in a URL has the same abuse issues as Lemon Ink; same mitigations (cap, filter, no links).
build.stage1MVP: Write a short note, pick two cities from a list, and get a tracking link that shows where Gerald the snail is now plus an 'add arrival to calendar' button.
build.portalFit: Poor: a weeks-long async loop doesn't fit portal sessions, and Playables bans network calls. Own site only.
fixes: Compute the snail from the timestamp; no backend.
Calendar-reminder (.ics) for arrival day.
Daily reason to check: a new diary line and a postcard per day, so the link is worth reopening.
Offer 'express' speeds (3 days) as the default so the payoff fits a TikTok attention span; keep 'real snail' as the joke mode.

ideas.title: Goodnight Town
ideas.hook: Put a cozy town to bed, light by light. Then it tells you to sleep.
ideas.oneLiner: Each night the little town's windows glow; you tap each house to finish its evening (kettle off, cat in, book closed) until every light is out and the game ends with 'goodnight, you too'.
ideas.fantasy: Being the gentle last-one-awake who makes sure everyone is tucked in.
ideas.coreLoop: Tap a lit window, do its 2-second bedtime micro-task, watch the light go out, repeat until the town is dark and the screen fades to stars.
ideas.howItSpreads: The 10-second clip of a town going dark window by window to lo-fi rain is instant ASMR/'sleepy TikTok' material; a spoiler-free 'last light out at 11:42pm' card; bedtime routine creators.
ideas.monetization: Free nightly town. $3 'Seasons' pack: snow town, harbor town, lantern-festival town, plus a sleep-sound mixer. Never sells extra play time; the game physically refuses to continue after lights-out.
ideas.whatsNew: Bounded play as the whole design: the win state is darkness and the 'that's enough for today' moment is the ending. Procedural households (who lives there, what they leave on) give nightly variety.
ideas.closestExisting: Bedtime-themed puzzle games (Bedtime Fright, Lights Out on itch.io) are about a scared kid avoiding the dark; this is a sleep ritual where darkness is the reward.
ideas.buildNotes: Very small: a single static town illustration in layers (one hand-drawn town per season), windows as procedurally lit rectangles with silhouettes, ~30 micro-task animations reused. No camera motion, so motion-sickness safe. Dark-mode by default.
cultureSignals: Digital detox, screen-time anxiety and 'brain rot' backlash
Romanticize your life, slow living, quiet life
ideas.verdictA: Sleep-ritual where darkness is the win; great sleepy clip, little native spread.
ideas.verdictB: Bedtime ritual where darkness wins is a strong concept; repeats quickly and doesn't spread.

ideas.title: Fold Together
ideas.hook: Two people, one phone, one fitted sheet. Fold it together without arguing.
ideas.oneLiner: Each person grabs two corners of a floppy cloth-physics sheet on the same phone and you must cooperate to fold laundry neatly, with a towel, tablecloth and, eventually, a giant duvet.
ideas.fantasy: The small domestic teamwork of couples and housemates, made silly and sweet.
ideas.coreLoop: Both players drag corners to match edges, the sheet snaps into a crisp fold with a satisfying thwump, and the basket slowly empties into a neat stack you can photograph.
ideas.howItSpreads: Couples filming each other fighting over a fitted sheet is a natural TikTok format; 'our fold score' card; works in person on a sofa, no link-pairing needed. Solo mode works with two thumbs.
ideas.monetization: Free basket of 10 items. $3 Laundry Day pack: patterned fabrics, a cat who lies on the sheet, a 'grandma's linen closet' mode with lace and quilts.
ideas.whatsNew: Two-player-one-screen multi-touch on phones is almost unused, and cloth physics gives emergent comedy. Directly answers the couples and co-op demand without netcode.
ideas.closestExisting: Highlaundry Overwashed (frantic Overcooked-style co-op laundry on Switch) and Flocks of Socks (20-second sock pairing); this is calm, untimed, cloth-physics folding on one shared phone.
ideas.buildNotes: Verlet cloth on a 2D grid is a well-known AI-codable system; multi-touch handling is the main work. Art is just fabric textures (patterns are cheap to make) plus a basket and a cat. Ship in days.
ideas.verdictA: Two people, one phone, fitted sheet: couples film themselves; no netcode.
ideas.verdictB: Two thumbs, one phone, fitted-sheet comedy: couples film themselves; needs more than ten items.
ideas.whySurvived: Fills the couples and co-op gap with a clip people will film themselves.
ideas.mainFix: Online pairing and a Discord Activity for long-distance players, a daily basket with one absurd item, and towel-animal folds to collect.
ideas.finalHook: Fold a fitted sheet with your partner. One phone. Try not to fight.

market.fatalFlaw: Four thumbs on one phone screen is cramped and needs two people physically together. Ten items are finished in 10 minutes, and there's no reason to play on day 2.
market.returnPlay: None as pitched. Fixed version: a daily basket, a linen-closet collection and towel-animal folds.
market.firstFrame: Overhead shot of a couple on a sofa, four thumbs on one phone, a floppy fitted sheet flailing. One says 'no, YOUR corner' and it snaps into a crisp square: thwump.
market.competitors: Highlaundry Overwashed (frantic co-op), Katazuke (multiplayer folding), Flocks of Socks, Unpacking (organizing satisfaction). The meme of couples failing to fold fitted sheets is the real competitor and the marketing.
fixes: Add link-pair online mode (each phone holds two corners, WebRTC) and a Discord Activity, so long-distance couples and friends can play.
Add a hotel-style fold progression ending in towel animals (swan, elephant, cat) that is collectible and photogenic, so folding has a reveal.
Add a linen closet that fills with your neat stacks as a persistent, decoratable shelf.
Add a daily 'laundry basket' (3 items, one absurd: an octopus costume, a parachute) with a shareable fold-score card.
Give it a tablet and desktop layout. Two people on an iPad is the real couch experience.
market.moneyPath: Free basket. $3 Laundry Day pack (fabrics, quilts, cat-on-sheet, towel animals). Strong Steam Couch Co-Op Fest candidate at $3-5 with controller support.
market.sharperHook: Fold a fitted sheet with your partner. One phone. Try not to fight.

build.hardestRisk: Folding is a 3D action faked in 2D: making layered cloth flaps read as a crisp fold (with no self-intersection mess) on a phone-sized screen with four thumbs at once.
build.needsServer: none. Local same-screen play; the score card is an image, and a 'same basket' challenge link is just a seed.
build.artLoad: low: tileable fabric patterns (could be photos/scans of real fabric), basket, cat. Very cheap.
build.mobileWebIssues: Four simultaneous touches on a phone is cramped. Test landscape and tablet. Must disable pinch-zoom, double-tap zoom and the iOS swipe-back gesture (touch-action:none, viewport user-scalable=no). Verlet cloth at ~20x20 is fine on low-end Android. No haptics on iOS for the 'thwump', so sound has to carry it.
build.stage1MVP: One towel and one fitted sheet: two players each drag two corners on one phone until it snaps into a fold, then get a 'fold score' card.
build.portalFit: Strong for Poki/CrazyGames if you add a desktop keyboard mode (WASD vs arrows): local 2-player is a big portal category. Playables fine (offline). Discord would need netcode, so later.
fixes: Add a share loop: 'challenge another couple' link with the same basket seed and a comparable score.
Add a desktop 2-player keyboard mode to unlock portals.
Make the fitted sheet a comedic 'boss' with springy corners; the cat lying on the sheet is the clip.
Solo two-thumb mode as default for TikTok visitors who are alone.

ideas.title: Night Feed
ideas.hook: A one-thumb, silent game for parents awake at 3am. You're not alone.
ideas.oneLiner: A dim, one-handed, sound-off game for new parents during night feeds: tend a moonlit garden while tiny lanterns show how many other parents are awake feeding right now.
ideas.fantasy: Quiet company in the loneliest hour; someone else is up too.
ideas.coreLoop: Swipe to water moonflowers and light a lantern; each feed grows the garden a little, and you can send a wordless 'you've got this' glow to another lantern before the baby falls asleep.
