ideas.howItSpreads: Shared in parenting group chats and NCT/antenatal WhatsApp groups ('for your 3am feeds'); clips of the counter ('2,318 parents awake with you'); baby-milestone garden snapshot to share in the morning.
ideas.monetization: Free forever core. $4 supporter pack: garden themes, a 'first year' keepsake garden timelapse printable as a poster, sibling/partner shared garden. Never ads (dark-screen, sleep-adjacent context).
ideas.whatsNew: Designs for a real, huge, under-served moment (night feeds) with hard constraints: one thumb, no sound, red-shifted low brightness, pause anywhere. Presence of strangers without chat makes it a third place.
ideas.closestExisting: Parents currently play generic Solitaire/2048/Cookie Clicker at 3am (per new-parent game roundups); body-doubling apps exist but none target night feeds with shared presence.
ideas.buildNotes: Small: a single garden scene with ~15 plant types growing in stages, simple realtime presence counter (one websocket or polling endpoint). Glows are pre-set, no text, so no moderation. Accessibility and darkness are the craft, not art volume.
cultureSignals: Loneliness epidemic and the search for low-cost third places
Gamified self-care and habit companions (Finch, Pokémon Sleep, Tamagotchi revival)
ideas.verdictA: Truly underserved moment and thoughtful constraints; niche, and no ads limits money.
ideas.verdictB: Real underserved moment with sharp constraints; narrow audience and nothing to film.

ideas.title: Chore Twin
ideas.hook: Tell it what chore you're doing. A tiny raccoon does the same chore beside you.
ideas.oneLiner: An ADHD body-double game: pick your real task (dishes, laundry, emails, tidying), and a small animal starts doing its own miniature version alongside you, finishing when you do.
ideas.fantasy: A loyal little co-worker who is just as reluctant as you but starts anyway.
ideas.coreLoop: Choose a chore and length, prop the phone up, your twin works (sighing, humming, occasionally getting distracted like you), then you both tap 'done' and its little home gets a bit cleaner too.
ideas.howItSpreads: Clip format: real sink of dishes beside a phone with a raccoon also washing tiny dishes. Share card: 'Me and Pickle did 4 loads of laundry today'. Live 'chore room' link shows other twins working right now.
ideas.monetization: Free: 1 twin, 8 chores. $4 pack: more twins (cat, frog, otter), more chores (taxes, studying, packing), a cozy home the twin decorates with earned items.
ideas.whatsNew: Body doubling usually means video of real people; this mirrors your specific task with a character, making the clip funny and the habit less lonely. Systemic idle animation, not content-heavy.
ideas.closestExisting: dubbii and FLOWN (human body-doubling sessions), Finch (self-care pet); none mirror the exact chore with a playful character twin.
ideas.buildNotes: Each chore is a looping 2-4 frame animation set per twin; start with 1 twin x 8 chores (~30 small animations). Code: timers, wake lock, optional presence room. Very solo-friendly.
cultureSignals: Focus timers and body doubling ('study with me', Forest, lofi streams)
CleanTok, organizing, restock and 'Sunday reset' content
ideas.verdictA: ADHD body-double raccoon mirrors your chore; clip with real sink is relatable.
ideas.verdictB: ADHD body double mirroring your chore is funny and sticky; sharing is only a card.

ideas.title: Rain Check
ideas.hook: A cafe that opens only when it's really raining. No rain? Visit someone else's.
ideas.oneLiner: A tiny rainy-window cafe tied to live weather: when it rains in your city you host; when it doesn't, you hop to a city where it's raining right now and sit in someone else's cafe.
ideas.fantasy: The perfect rainy afternoon, always available somewhere on Earth.
ideas.coreLoop: Check the live rain map, sit by a window in a rainy city, sip, collect a postcard of that rain (Lisbon drizzle, Mumbai monsoon), and fill a rain journal; real rain at home unlocks hosting and its own ingredients.
ideas.howItSpreads: 'It's raining in my city, come sit in my cafe' link; daily clip 'where is it raining right now'; rain journal grid as a share card; rain ASMR natural for TikTok.
ideas.monetization: Free. $3 supporter pack: cafe decor sets, rain sound mixer, umbrella collection, a 'rain alarm' notification for when it starts raining near you.
ideas.whatsNew: Real-world weather as the scarcity and daily cadence instead of an artificial timer; turns other cities' rain into tourism and connection. Content is generated by the planet.
ideas.closestExisting: Ame no Furu Hoshi (progresses only during real rain), Lovely Weather We're Having (mirrors local weather); neither makes rain a shared, visitable social place.
ideas.buildNotes: Open-Meteo free API for precipitation by city; one hand-painted cafe window scene with swappable outside skylines (simple silhouettes per region). Rain is particles + sound. Presence via light polling.
cultureSignals: Romanticize your life, slow living, quiet life
ideas.verdictA: Real rain as scarcity is nice; visiting strangers' cafés is thin play.
ideas.verdictB: Rain as real-world scarcity is clever, but the loop is mostly sitting and presence is thin.

ideas.title: Dawn Chorus
ideas.hook: Listen at your window and learn the birds by ear. Mostly played eyes closed.
ideas.oneLiner: A mostly-listening game: each morning a real-recorded dawn chorus plays from a window, and you gently name the birds by their songs to fill a hand-drawn field notebook.
ideas.fantasy: Becoming the person who says 'oh, that's a wren' on a walk.
ideas.coreLoop: Listen to today's 60-second chorus, tap the song you hear to pin it, guess from a few soft choices, and a bird sketch appears in your notebook; the chorus gets richer as you learn more voices.
ideas.howItSpreads: Daily spoiler-free card ('heard 5 of 7 this morning' with notebook doodles); 'can you name this bird?' audio clips; birding and nature TikTok are large and older-skewing.
ideas.monetization: Free daily chorus. $4 region packs (UK garden, US east, Japan, Australia) and a night-chorus pack (owls, frogs). License-clean recordings (CC0/CC-BY xeno-canto, credited).
ideas.whatsNew: Audio as the core input in a cozy daily; zero motion so motion-sickness safe; appeals to older adults and non-gamers. Real-world data gives effectively infinite content.
ideas.closestExisting: Merlin Bird ID (a tool, not a game) and bird-quiz sites; this is a daily cozy ritual with a collectible notebook and gentle difficulty.
ideas.buildNotes: Mixing recordings into a chorus is code; art is ~50 hand-drawn bird sketches per region (can be pencil-simple, the style is 'field notebook'). Licensing care is the main human task.
cultureSignals: Cozy games for older adults / accessibility-first
'Grandma hobbies' and the analog crafting revival
ideas.verdictA: Good older-adult daily; audio-only content is weak on silent feeds.
ideas.verdictB: Good for older players and daily, but audio-first kills muted clips.

ideas.title: Helpful Ghost
ideas.hook: You're the ghost. Your new roommate is having a bad day. Haunt them nicely.
ideas.oneLiner: A cozy-spooky room puzzle where you are an invisible ghost secretly nudging objects to make a nervous tenant's day go well: warm the tea, find the keys, open the window for the cat.
ideas.fantasy: Kindness without credit; being someone's guardian in their own home.
ideas.coreLoop: Each day the tenant has a small worry; you poke, float and tilt objects in one room to solve it without being seen, and the tenant slowly decorates the house (and leaves you a cookie).
ideas.howItSpreads: Inverted-horror premise makes a great caption; clips of the ghost frantically pushing keys into view while the tenant isn't looking; October launch with cute-spooky skin.
ideas.monetization: Free first week of days. $3 unlock for the full year of the tenant's life (job interview, first date, new kitten) plus ghost hats.
ideas.whatsNew: Flips haunting into care; the comedy of near-misses (tenant almost sees you) gives streamer drama without fail states (being seen just makes them shrug).
ideas.closestExisting: Ghost-help games like Lamplighter's Rest (on the list: you help ghosts) and Untitled Goose Game (prankster in someone's space); here you are the ghost and the mischief is benevolent.
ideas.buildNotes: One room at a time, fixed camera, ~20 interactive props per room with simple physics. Tenant needs ~10 poses. Daily puzzles are small authored setups; reuse rooms with prop variations.
cultureSignals: Cozy games with a darker or mysterious edge (Dredge-like)
ideas.verdictA: Benevolent-ghost caption plus October timing; authored puzzles cost writing time.
ideas.verdictB: Kind-haunting premise and near-miss comedy fit October; authored daily puzzles are costly.

ideas.title: Hand-Me-Downs
ideas.hook: You own 40 lovely things. Win by giving every single one away.
ideas.oneLiner: An anti-hoarding collection game: you start with a full shelf of plush keepsakes and gently figure out which neighbor would love each one most, ending with an empty shelf and a happy street.
ideas.fantasy: Letting go generously; the warmth of the perfect gift.
ideas.coreLoop: Read a neighbor's little clues (window, mailbox, what they hum), pick an item off your shelf, gift it, and see it appear in their home and life; wrong guesses still get a kind thank-you and a hint.
ideas.howItSpreads: Silhouette shelf emptying is the inverse of blind-box shelves and reads instantly; share card shows your street with all gifts placed; clip of a grumpy neighbor lighting up.
ideas.monetization: Free street 1. $3 for new streets (seaside, snowy, city block). Seasonal gift-giving streets at Christmas/Valentine's.
ideas.whatsNew: Inverts the collecting trend (Pop Mart, Labubu) into a game about giving; deduction puzzle with emotional payoff. Uses the same plush-object style the creator already needs for Treat Box, so assets cross over.
ideas.closestExisting: Unpacking (placing belongings), Is This Seat Taken? (matching people to seats); this is matching gifts to people as a giving-away arc with no hoarding at all.
ideas.buildNotes: Each street: ~10 neighbors (simple house facades + 1 character portrait) and ~40 plush items; clue system is data-driven so AI-assisted code can generate many puzzle permutations from tags.
cultureSignals: Blind boxes, Pop Mart and Labubu
Kidult collecting (adults buying toys for themselves)
ideas.verdictA: Giving-away inversion is warm; deduction puzzles need lots of authored clues.
ideas.verdictB: Clever inversion of collecting, but a one-time deduction arc with no clip or spread.

ideas.title: Bench Pigeon
ideas.hook: You're a pigeon on a park bench. People sit down and tell you things.
ideas.oneLiner: A mostly-listening, absurd-but-warm game: as a pigeon, you choose a bench, strangers sit and talk about their day, and you coo, nod or share your crust; their stories quietly interlink.
ideas.fantasy: Being the confidant everyone needs, with zero social pressure.
ideas.coreLoop: Hop to a bench, listen to a 1-minute monologue, react with coos, collect the little item they leave behind, and notice the next day's visitor is connected (the widow's grandson, the nervous intern's boss).
ideas.howItSpreads: Clip: a pigeon cooing sympathetically at a man rehearsing a proposal. Players share favourite lines. Placid Plastic Duck-style 'what is this' charm for streamers.
ideas.monetization: Free first season (10 visitors). $3 for each new park (seaside promenade, train station, winter market) with new interlinked stories.
ideas.whatsNew: Narrative delivered through listening instead of dialogue trees; the absurd point of view makes heartfelt writing land without being preachy.
ideas.closestExisting: Placid Plastic Duck Simulator (watch, absurd-warm), Is This Seat Taken? (characters on seats), Kind Words (listening to strangers); none put you as the silent animal confidant.
ideas.buildNotes: Writing is the main human craft (short monologues, human-written). Art: one park bench scene, ~10 visitor silhouettes with simple 2-frame gestures, a very expressive pigeon. Optional human voice-over later.
cultureSignals: Loneliness epidemic and the search for low-cost third places
Absurd escalation / premise as the hook
ideas.verdictA: Absurd-warm pigeon confidant; writing-heavy narrative cozy is harder to sell.
ideas.verdictB: Pigeon confidant is a great caption, but narrative cozy is consumed once and sells poorly.

ideas.title: Puzzle Postcard
ideas.hook: Don't send grandma a photo. Send her a jigsaw of it.
ideas.oneLiner: Turn any photo into a big-piece jigsaw link for a grandparent (or anyone); they solve it, the picture is revealed, and they reply with a sticker and a one-tap voice note.
ideas.fantasy: A small gift that takes a few minutes to unwrap, from someone who loves you.
ideas.coreLoop: Sender picks a photo and piece count (9 to 100), adds a hidden message under the last piece; recipient assembles it with large, forgiving pieces and replies; both build a shared album of solved postcards.
ideas.howItSpreads: Every play is a share; players create the content. Clips of grandparents reacting when the final piece reveals the grandchild's message ('I'm pregnant', 'we got a dog').
ideas.monetization: Free 3 postcards a week. $4 family pack: unlimited postcards, piece shapes (hearts, leaves), frame styles, printable solved-puzzle keepsakes.
ideas.whatsNew: Accessibility-first for older adults (huge pieces, no timers, high contrast, no motion) and a reveal mechanic for announcements; it is a gift ritual, not a puzzle library.
ideas.closestExisting: Jigsaw Planet and photo-puzzle apps let you make puzzles from photos; they are puzzle libraries, not gift-and-reply rituals designed for grandparents with a hidden reveal message.
ideas.buildNotes: Pure code: jigsaw cut generation, drag/snap, storage of user images (privacy: unlisted links, auto-expiry). Almost zero bespoke art: frames, stickers and a cozy table texture.
cultureSignals: Cozy games for older adults / accessibility-first
Unboxing / mystery-reveal as a content format
ideas.verdictA: Photo jigsaw exists; reveal-message angle is nice but image storage adds risk.
ideas.verdictB: Photo jigsaws exist; the reveal-message gift is good but user photos add privacy load.

ideas.title: Leaf Poems
ideas.hook: Today's words fall like autumn leaves. Rake them into a tiny poem.
ideas.oneLiner: A typography-led daily: the same 20 hand-picked words drift down for everyone each day; you rake and arrange them into a three-line poem and see a gallery of what others wrote.
ideas.fantasy: A quiet creative minute; making something lovely out of what fell your way.
ideas.coreLoop: Leaves with words fall, you gather the ones you like into a pile, drag them into three lines, press 'pin to the tree', then browse other poems from the same words and give leaves to favourites.
ideas.howItSpreads: Each poem exports as a pretty leaf card for Stories; 'same words, different poems' is a Connections-style shared topic; poetry TikTok is large.
ideas.monetization: Free daily. $3 supporter pack: seasonal word sets (winter snowflakes, spring petals), paper and ink styles, a printable yearly zine of your poems.
ideas.whatsNew: Magnetic-poetry creativity plus daily shared scarcity and a gallery; the art is typography and one falling-leaf system, so it is cheap to make and visually distinct.
ideas.closestExisting: Magnetic poetry apps and Wordle-style dailies; this is creative not competitive, with a shared word set and community gallery.
ideas.buildNotes: Leaf physics + drag-and-arrange; gallery with simple moderation (word set is fixed, so offensive output is limited). Art: a few leaf shapes and a hand-drawn tree; fonts do the rest.
ideas.verdictA: Magnetic poetry daily; gallery needs moderation and clip is static.
ideas.verdictB: Typography-cheap daily, but poetry galleries need moderation and appeal narrowly.

ideas.title: Bottle Drift
ideas.hook: Throw a message in a bottle. Real ocean currents carry it to a stranger.
ideas.oneLiner: Seal a doodle or kind phrase in a bottle, toss it from your nearest coast, and watch it drift on simulated real currents for days until it washes up on someone's beach across the world.
ideas.fantasy: Romantic chance; something from far away chose you.
ideas.coreLoop: Comb your beach each day for washed-up bottles and shells, read and keep what you find, reply by sending your own bottle, and check the drift map to see where yours is now.
ideas.howItSpreads: Clips of opening a bottle that drifted 9 days from Chile; drift-map screenshots; 'my bottle just landed in Japan' shares from players tracking theirs.
ideas.monetization: Free 1 bottle a day. $3 pack: glass colors, corks, beach decor, a 'lighthouse' that tells you when your bottle lands.
ideas.whatsNew: Real ocean current data (e.g. NOAA/OSCAR surface currents) as the content engine; fills the cozy ocean lane; strangers connect without chat.
ideas.closestExisting: Kind Words (letters to strangers) and Slowly; neither use real ocean drift as delivery or a beachcombing loop. Searches found no browser game simulating real-current bottles.
ideas.buildNotes: Particle advection on a coarse current grid is straightforward code. Messages: sticker phrase-builder + doodle with report button to keep it safe. Art: one beach scene, bottle variants, ~30 shells.
cultureSignals: Loneliness epidemic and the search for low-cost third places
Unboxing / mystery-reveal as a content format
ideas.verdictA: Same as Driftmail with riskier phrase/doodle messaging.
ideas.verdictB: Same as Driftmail with a clearer hook; free phrases raise moderation load.

ideas.title: Drizzle
ideas.hook: You're a small rain cloud. The village needs exactly the right amount of you.
ideas.oneLiner: Play as a little cloud drifting over a procedural village: water gardens, fill puddles for kids in boots, cool the baker, and avoid the picnic, ending each day in a rainbow.
ideas.fantasy: Being weather, and being welcome.
ideas.coreLoop: Drag the cloud and hold to rain; each villager has a gentle wish (wet tomatoes, a puddle to jump in, dry laundry), granting them blooms the village, and a full day ends with a rainbow photo.
ideas.howItSpreads: Clips of a cloud lovingly raining on a single sunflower, or a dog shaking off; the end-of-day rainbow photo as share card; whimsical premise in one caption.
ideas.monetization: Free. $3 pack: snow cloud, fog, thunder (gentle drums), new villages (rice terraces, a harbor), cloud faces and hats.
ideas.whatsNew: Inverts the player from inhabitant to weather; the systemic village (needs, moisture, growth) makes emergent little stories without a script.
ideas.closestExisting: Rain-cloud casual mobile games and god-games like From Dust (much harsher); this is a cozy no-fail weather-as-caretaker toy.
ideas.buildNotes: Tile-based moisture sim plus particle rain; 2D side or top view with a fixed camera. Art: ~12 villager types, 3 tile sets, an expressive cloud. Procedural village layouts reduce hand work.
cultureSignals: Studio Ghibli aesthetic demand and the 2025 AI 'Ghibli filter' backlash
ideas.verdictA: Be the rain cloud is charming; village sim must be authored to feel alive.
ideas.verdictB: Being a helpful cloud is instantly charming; the needs-sim must stay interesting beyond day one.

ideas.title: The House Remembers
ideas.hook: You are a house. Families come and go for a hundred years.
ideas.oneLiner: A timelapse life-sim where the player is the house: each tap is a season, families move in, grow, repaint you, leave, and you choose small comforts (a warm floor, a creak that wakes someone in time).
ideas.fantasy: The quiet continuity of home; being loved by people who never knew each other.
ideas.coreLoop: Advance a season, watch the procedural household's moment, spend 'warmth' on a tiny intervention, and see the marks they leave (height lines on the doorframe) accumulate across generations.
ideas.howItSpreads: Before/after of one room over 100 years is a perfect vertical timelapse; the ending 'house biography' card is unique to each player and shareable.
ideas.monetization: Free first house. $4 for new houses (seaside cottage, city apartment, farmhouse in Japan) and an extended century mode.
ideas.whatsNew: Bittersweet-but-cozy inversion about time and letting go; procedural families mean each run differs, so it is replayable without heavy writing.
ideas.closestExisting: What Remains of Edith Finch and Unpacking (stories through homes); this is a systemic, replayable, you-are-the-house timelapse.
ideas.buildNotes: One cross-section house in a single fixed view; decor sets by era (~6 eras) swapped procedurally; people as simple silhouettes. Event generator is code-heavy, art-light.
cultureSignals: Romanticize your life, slow living, quiet life
Cozy games with a darker or mysterious edge (Dredge-like)
ideas.verdictA: Beautiful timelapse premise; meaningful procedural families are hard to build.
ideas.verdictB: Century timelapse is moving, but procedural narrative that lands is hard and it's played once.

ideas.title: Plane Spotting Porch
ideas.hook: Sit on your porch. Wave at the real planes flying over you right now.
ideas.oneLiner: A real-data ambient game: live flight data shows the actual planes passing over your town; tap to wave, guess where they're going, and collect a stamp for each real destination.
ideas.fantasy: Childhood wonder at the sky; tiny connections with strangers going somewhere.
ideas.coreLoop: Open the porch, see the next real plane drift across the sky, wave, pick its destination from three postcards, and fill a passport of places that flew over you.
ideas.howItSpreads: 'Everyone over Manchester just got waved at by me' clips; passport grid as share card; plane-spotting and aviation communities; a 'wave back' feature for players on board with in-flight wifi.
ideas.monetization: Free. $3 pack: night sky mode, porch decor, rare liveries album, a long-haul 'collect every continent' book.
ideas.whatsNew: Uses real flight data as infinite daily content; leave-it-running but anchored to your actual sky. Contrarian 'it's the planes, not you, that move' format.
ideas.closestExisting: Flightradar24 (a tool) and plane-spotting apps; none frame it as a cozy, wave-and-collect porch toy.
ideas.buildNotes: OpenSky/ADS-B public APIs (check rate limits/terms; city-level location only). Art: one porch with sky gradient by real time, a handful of plane silhouettes, stamp designs that can be typographic.

ideas.title: Fridge Door
ideas.hook: A shared fridge door for your household, even when you live apart.
ideas.oneLiner: A link-shared fridge for couples, families or long-distance friends: leave magnets, poetry, doodles and tiny chores; every morning the fridge reveals what the others stuck on it overnight.
ideas.fantasy: The warm clutter of a family kitchen, wherever everyone is.
ideas.coreLoop: Open the fridge, see new notes, rearrange the magnet-poetry, stick a doodle or a sticker you earned, and complete the day's little magnet set (collect the full fruit alphabet together).
ideas.howItSpreads: The fridge link is the invite; screenshots of a cluttered shared fridge are perfect for Stories; couples and long-distance-friend TikTok.
ideas.monetization: Free for 2 people. $4 household pack: up to 6 people, magnet series (open odds, earned not bought), fridge colors, a 'year on the fridge' printable collage.
ideas.whatsNew: Couples and families lane with a cozy shared object instead of a chat app; the morning reveal is a daily ritual and the magnets are a soft collection.
ideas.closestExisting: Locket widget and shared-note apps (utility), Pond Party (live shared space); this is an asynchronous household object with collectible magnets.
ideas.buildNotes: Simple real-time doc (one JSON per fridge). Art: one fridge, ~80 small magnet designs (letters can be typographic). Privacy is easy: invite-only links, no public content.
cultureSignals: Kidult collecting (adults buying toys for themselves)
Unboxing / mystery-reveal as a content format
ideas.verdictA: Shared fridge for couples/families is clear and sticky; little to film.
ideas.verdictB: Shared household fridge suits couples; doodles need care and screenshots are its only clip.

ideas.title: Pass the Scarf
ideas.hook: Knit ten stitches on a stranger's scarf. Get told when it's finished.
ideas.oneLiner: A slow relay craft: you receive a half-knitted scarf from a stranger, add your ten rows in your colors and pattern, pass it on, and get a link when your scarf is completed by a hundred hands.
ideas.fantasy: Being part of something made by many quiet strangers.
ideas.coreLoop: Receive a scarf, see its history by colors, knit your rows with a rhythmic tap pattern, add a tiny charm, pass it on; check your 'scarves I touched' wall for finished ones.
ideas.howItSpreads: Finished scarves are gorgeous long scroll-down clips ('100 strangers made this'); each completion pings every contributor, bringing them back; shareable 'my rows' highlight.
ideas.monetization: Free. $3 supporter pack: yarn colors, stitch patterns, charm sets, start-your-own-scarf with a theme for friends/classes. Possible real knitted-by-hand print merch later.
ideas.whatsNew: Async relay with strangers (like r/place but slow and kind), with a payoff notification weeks later; procedural knit rendering means no bespoke art per scarf.
ideas.closestExisting: Quilt Porch (on the list, solo quilts), r/place (live pixel canvas), exquisite-corpse games; this is a slow, wordless stranger relay with a completion reveal.
ideas.buildNotes: Knit renderer from stitch grid (shader or canvas), queue of scarves on a server. Art: yarn textures and ~30 charms. Moderation minimal (patterns only, no text).
cultureSignals: 'Grandma hobbies' and the analog crafting revival (crochet, knitting, embroidery, junk journals)
Loneliness epidemic and the search for low-cost third places
ideas.verdictA: Stranger relay knitting; weaker than Pass the Blanket's friend chain.
ideas.verdictB: Stranger scarf relay; weaker than Pass the Blanket, which travels through friends.

ideas.title: Steep
ideas.hook: Set your tea's real steep time. A tiny scene ends when your tea does.
ideas.oneLiner: A cozy game sized to your real waiting moments: tell it you're steeping tea (3 min), waiting for pasta (9 min) or the bus (6 min), and it plays a calm scene that ends exactly on time.
ideas.fantasy: Making little waits feel like small treats instead of doomscrolling.
ideas.coreLoop: Pick your real wait, play a self-contained cozy micro-scene (tend a moss jar, sort buttons, watch a fox nap) that resolves with a gentle chime at the end, collect the scene's keepsake.
ideas.howItSpreads: Clip: real mug of tea next to the phone, both finishing together; tea and morning-routine creators; share card 'my waits this week: 41 minutes of moss'.
ideas.monetization: Free 3 scenes. $3 one-time pack: 20 more scenes, a 'kettle shelf' of keepsakes and custom chime sounds.
ideas.whatsNew: Time-boxed by the player's real life instead of the game's energy meter; replaces doomscrolling in micro-gaps, an anti-brain-rot pitch with a concrete use.
ideas.closestExisting: Kitchen timers and Forest (focus timer); this is a library of exact-length cozy toys that finish when your real-world wait finishes.
ideas.buildNotes: Each scene is a small procedural toy that stretches to any duration; ship with 5-6 scenes. Art per scene is small (one hand-painted vignette). Solo-friendly, expandable over time.
cultureSignals: Digital detox, screen-time anxiety and 'brain rot' backlash

ideas.verdictA: Real-wait-sized scenes is a smart use case; each scene still needs art.

ideas.title: Odd Sock Dating
ideas.hook: Every lost sock deserves love. Run a matchmaking agency for single socks.
ideas.oneLiner: An absurd-warm matchmaking puzzle: lonely odd socks arrive with personality profiles, and you pair them with other odd socks who aren't their twin but are perfect for them.
ideas.fantasy: Running a tiny, deeply sincere matchmaking agency for laundry.
ideas.coreLoop: Read sock profiles (wool, loves hiking, afraid of dryers), seat pairs on dates in the laundromat cafe, watch the comedic date animation, and pin happy couples to the corkboard; mismatched dates are funny, never failures.
ideas.howItSpreads: Sock profiles are screenshot gold ('Argyle, 47, seeks sock who won't shrink'); date clips; players share their weirdest successful couple; 'what's your sock's personality' quiz link.
ideas.monetization: Free first week of clients. $3 pack: new client batches, a wedding chapel where socks get married, seasonal socks (Christmas stocking clients).
ideas.whatsNew: Absurd-premise caption hook (Placid Duck energy) married to a systemic tag-based matching puzzle that produces endless funny pairings with little writing.
ideas.closestExisting: Is This Seat Taken? (matching characters to seats), dating sims; this is low-stakes matchmaking with socks and procedural profiles.
ideas.buildNotes: Socks are simple shapes with pattern textures and procedural profiles from tag tables (human-written phrase banks). One laundromat cafe scene. Very cheap art, mostly writing jokes.
cultureSignals: Absurd escalation / premise as the hook
ideas.verdictA: Sock dating profiles are screenshot gold; Is This Seat Taken-adjacent matching.
ideas.verdictB: Sock dating profiles are screenshot jokes; humour writing must carry a shallow matching loop.
